knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence and flat-rank exactness of generalized moment relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic value convergence and conditional finite atomic recovery for the primal-dual SDP hierarchy of a generalized moment problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{f,(h_j)_{j\in\Gamma},(g_j)_{j=1}^m\}\subset\mathbb R[\mathbf x]\), let \(\mathbb K\subset\mathbb R^n\) be as in the generalized moment model, assume \(h_0>0\) on \(\mathbb K\), Assumption 2.1 holds, and the generalized moment problem has finite optimal value \(\rho_{\mathrm{mom}}\). For the primal and dual SDP relaxation values \((\rho_i)_i\) and \((\rho_i^*)_i\), \(\rho_i\downarrow\rho_{\mathrm{mom}}\) and \(\rho_i^*\downarrow\rho_{\mathrm{mom}}\). If the level-\(i\) primal relaxation has an optimal solution \(\mathbf y\) satisfying \(\operatorname{rank}M_s(\mathbf y)=\operatorname{rank}M_{s-v}(\mathbf y)\) for some \(i_0\le s\le i\), where \(v=\max_jv_j\), then \(\rho_i=\rho_{\mathrm{mom}}\), and the generalized moment problem has an optimal measure \(\mu\in\mathcal M(\mathbb K)_+\) finitely supported on \(\operatorname{rank}M_s(\mathbf y)\) points of \(\mathbb K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated positivity, regularity, and finite-value assumptions, the primal and dual SDP relaxation values both decrease to the generalized moment optimum. If an optimal primal relaxation solution satisfies the flat-rank condition, that relaxation is exact and the moment problem has an optimal finitely supported measure with as many support points as the indicated moment-matrix rank.
assumptions_latex: \mathbf y\text{ is an optimal solution of the level-}i\text{ primal relaxation for part (b)}
\operatorname{rank}M_s(\mathbf y)=\operatorname{rank}M_{s-v}(\mathbf y)\text{ for some }i_0\le s\le i,\quad v=\max_jv_j
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho_i^*\downarrow\rho_{\mathrm{mom}},\quad\rho_i\downarrow\rho_{\mathrm{mom}};\qquad \operatorname{rank}M_s(\mathbf y)=\operatorname{rank}M_{s-v}(\mathbf y)\Rightarrow \rho_i=\rho_{\mathrm{mom}}\text{ and }\exists\mu\in\mathcal M(\mathbb K)_+\text{ optimal, finitely supported on }\operatorname{rank}M_s(\mathbf y)\text{ points}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine moment constraints and objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: GloptiPoly representation of finite generalized-moment models involving labeled measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given labeled measures \(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_s\), GloptiPoly permits affine equalities and inequalities that combine moments from several measures, of the form \(\sum_{j=1}^m a_j\int p_j\,d\mu_{k_j}\ \bowtie\ b\), where \(\bowtie\in\{=,\le,\ge\}\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generalized moment problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finitely constrained linear optimization over nonnegative measures supported on a prescribed set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(f_0,f_1,\ldots,f_N\in\mathbb R[x]\), \(a_1,\ldots,a_N\in\mathbb R\), and a support set \(K\), the generalized moment problem is \[\operatorname{val}:=\inf_{\mu\in\mathcal M(K)}\left\{\int_K f_0(x)\,d\mu:\int_K f_i(x)\,d\mu=a_i\quad(i\in[N])\right\}.\] The probability-measure reformulation of polynomial optimization is the special case \(N=1\) and \(f_1=a_1=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generalized moment problem optimizes a polynomial integral over nonnegative measures supported on K subject to finitely many prescribed polynomial moments. The probability-measure formulation of polynomial optimization is its normalization-only special case.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{val}=\inf_{\mu\in\mathcal M(K)}\left\{\int_K f_0\,d\mu:\int_K f_i\,d\mu=a_i\ (i\in[N])\right\}

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Measure Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized moment problem with one unknown nonnegative measure and linear integral constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\) be a measurable space, let \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m,h_1,\ldots,h_r\) be measurable real-valued functions, and let \(a\in\mathbb R^m\), \(b\in\mathbb R^r\). A single-measure generalized moment model is
\[
\inf_{\mu\in\mathcal M_+(K)}\left\{\int_K f\,d\mu:\ \int_K g_i\,d\mu=a_i\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ \int_K h_j\,d\mu\le b_j\ (j=1,\ldots,r)\right\},
\]
where every displayed integral is finite. Prescribing \(\int_K1\,d\mu=1\) restricts the variable to probability measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single-measure model optimizes a linear integral over one nonnegative measure subject to prescribed moment equalities and inequalities.
assumptions_latex: All integrals occurring in the objective and constraints are well-defined and finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimization variable is one measure \(\mu\in\mathcal M_+(K)\), and the objective and constraints are linear in \(\mu\).

notation.meaning: Cone of finite nonnegative measures on K satisfying the required integrability conditions.
Moment of the function q under the measure μ.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-Measure Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized moment problem whose linear constraints couple finitely many nonnegative measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(s,m,r\in\mathbb N\), let \(K_1,\ldots,K_s\) be measurable spaces, and, for the indicated indices, let \(f_j,g_{ij},h_{\ell j}:K_j\to\mathbb R\) be measurable. Let \(a\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^r\). A multiple-measure generalized moment model has variables \(\mu_j\in\mathcal M_+(K_j)\) and the form
\[
\inf_{\mu_j\in\mathcal M_+(K_j),\ 1\le j\le s}\left\{\sum_{j=1}^s\int_{K_j}f_j\,d\mu_j:\ \sum_{j=1}^s\int_{K_j}g_{ij}\,d\mu_j=a_i\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ \sum_{j=1}^s\int_{K_j}h_{\ell j}\,d\mu_j\le b_\ell\ (\ell=1,\ldots,r)\right\},
\]
where every displayed integral is finite. Each objective or constraint is a linear functional of the product variable \((\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_s)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiple-measure model linearly optimizes over finitely many nonnegative measures, with constraints allowed to couple their moments.
assumptions_latex: Every displayed integral is well-defined and finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model is a linear program over \(\prod_{j=1}^s\mathcal M_+(K_j)\).

notation.meaning: Underlying measurable space of the j-th measure.
Cone of finite nonnegative measures on K_j satisfying the displayed integrability requirements.
The j-th finite nonnegative measure.

knowledge_statements.title: Finitely Constrained Moment Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment models having a finite list of linear equality and inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\) be a measurable space, let \(I\) and \(J\) be finite index sets, let \(f\), \((g_i)_{i\in I}\), and \((h_j)_{j\in J}\) be measurable real-valued functions on \(K\), and let \((a_i)_{i\in I}\) and \((b_j)_{j\in J}\) be real scalars. A finitely constrained moment model is
\[
\inf_{\mu\in\mathcal M_+(K)}\left\{\int_K f\,d\mu:\ \int_K g_i\,d\mu=a_i\ (i\in I),\ \int_K h_j\,d\mu\le b_j\ (j\in J)\right\},
\]
where all displayed integrals are finite. Its feasibility and objective value depend on finitely many moment coordinates; equalities may equivalently be represented by pairs of inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finitely constrained moment model uses only finitely many linear moment equalities and inequalities, so its objective and feasibility depend on finitely many moment coordinates.
assumptions_latex: All displayed integrals are well-defined and finite for admissible measures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility and the objective value are determined by finitely many coordinates of \(\mu\).

notation.meaning: Finite index sets for equality and inequality constraints.
Cone of finite nonnegative measures on K satisfying the displayed integrability requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Countably Constrained Moment Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment models with constraints indexed by a countably infinite set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\) be a measurable space, let \(f:K\to\mathbb R\) and \(g_i:K\to\mathbb R\) for \(i\in\mathbb N\) be measurable, and let \((a_i)_{i\in\mathbb N}\subset\mathbb R\). A countably constrained moment model is
\[
\inf_{\mu\in\mathcal M_+(K)}\left\{\int_K f\,d\mu:\ \int_K g_i\,d\mu=a_i\ \text{for every }i\in\mathbb N\right\},
\]
where the required integrals are finite; countably indexed inequalities may be included analogously. For \(n\ge1\), define
\[
F_n:=\left\{\mu\in\mathcal M_+(K):\int_K g_i\,d\mu=a_i\ \text{for }i=1,\ldots,n\right\}.
\]
The feasible set of the full equality system is \(\bigcap_{n\ge1}F_n\). Nonemptiness of every \(F_n\) does not by itself imply that this intersection is nonempty without an additional compactness or tightness condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A countably constrained model imposes infinitely many moment conditions. Its feasible set is the intersection of the finite truncation sets, which may all be nonempty even when their full intersection is empty.
assumptions_latex: All required integrals are well-defined and finite for admissible measures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The full feasible set is \(\bigcap_{n\ge1}F_n\), where \(F_n\) imposes the first \(n\) constraints.

notation.meaning: Feasible set for the first n moment constraints.
Countable constraint index set.
Cone of finite nonnegative measures on K satisfying the required integrability conditions.

children.title: Primal-Dual Representation Family
children.top_down_role: Measure-space, moment-coordinate, and positivity-dual views of generalized moment models.

knowledge_statements.title: Measure-Space Linear Programs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic linear representation of generalized moment problems directly over nonnegative measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\) be compact Hausdorff, let \(m\in\mathbb N\), let \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in C(K)\), and let \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). Define \(A:\mathcal M(K)\to\mathbb R^m\) by \((A\mu)_i=\int_K g_i\,d\mu\). The equality-constrained generalized moment problem is the conic linear program
\[
p^*=\inf\left\{\langle f,\mu\rangle:A\mu=b,\ \mu\in\mathcal M_+(K)\right\},
\]
where \(\langle f,\mu\rangle=\int_K f\,d\mu\). Linear inequalities can be incorporated using nonnegative slack variables or finite-dimensional conic constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equality-constrained generalized moment problem is a conic linear program whose variable lies in the cone of nonnegative measures; linear inequalities can be added through slack or conic variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The moment problem is represented as \(\inf\{\langle f,\mu\rangle:A\mu=b,\ \mu\in\mathcal M_+(K)\}\).

notation.meaning: Continuous real-valued functions on K.
Finite signed regular Borel measures on K.
Cone of finite nonnegative regular Borel measures on K.
Finite-dimensional moment map.

knowledge_statements.title: Moment-Coordinate Programs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional conic reformulation using moments of the functions appearing in the model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\) be compact Hausdorff, let \(q_0,\ldots,q_d\in C(K)\), and define
\[
T\mu:=\left(\int_Kq_0\,d\mu,\ldots,\int_Kq_d\,d\mu\right),\qquad C_q:=T(\mathcal M_+(K)).
\]
Let \(p,r\) be nonnegative integers, \(c\in\mathbb R^{d+1}\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{p\times(d+1)}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), \(D\in\mathbb R^{r\times(d+1)}\), and \(e\in\mathbb R^r\). If a measure-space model has objective \(c^\mathsf T T\mu\) and constraints \(BT\mu=b\) and \(DT\mu\le e\), then it is equivalently represented by
\[
\inf_{y\in C_q}\left\{c^\mathsf Ty:By=b,\ Dy\le e\right\}.
\]
The two formulations have identical feasible objective values because \(y\in C_q\) means that \(y=T\mu\) for at least one nonnegative measure \(\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Collecting the required integrals into a moment vector converts a measure model that factors through those integrals into a finite-dimensional linear program over the attainable moment cone.
assumptions_latex: The objective and every constraint factor through \(T\).
The matrices and vectors have the displayed finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The measure formulation and the program over \(C_q\) have identical feasible objective values and the same infimum.

notation.meaning: Moment-coordinate map from measures to Euclidean space.
Cone of moment vectors attainable by nonnegative measures.
Finite moment-coordinate vector in R^{d+1}.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Positivity Programs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrange dual of an equality-constrained measure linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\) be compact Hausdorff, let \(m\in\mathbb N\), let \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_m\in C(K)\), and let \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). For the primal problem
\[
p^*:=\inf_{\mu\in\mathcal M_+(K)}\left\{\int_K f\,d\mu:\int_K g_i\,d\mu=b_i\ (i=1,\ldots,m)\right\},
\]
the Lagrange dual is
\[
\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^m}\left\{b^\mathsf T\lambda:f-\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i g_i\ge0\ \text{on }K\right\}.
\]
Every dual-feasible \(\lambda\) satisfies the weak-duality bound \(b^\mathsf T\lambda\le p^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual multipliers maximize a linear lower bound while requiring the objective function minus their constraint combination to be nonnegative on the support set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed positivity program is the Lagrange dual, and every primal-feasible \(\mu\) and dual-feasible \(\lambda\) satisfy \(b^\mathsf T\lambda\le\int_K f\,d\mu\).

notation.meaning: Vector of equality-constraint multipliers.
Dual residual required to be nonnegative on K.
Cone of finite nonnegative regular Borel measures on K.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weak and Strong Duality for the Generalized Moment Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak duality, together with sufficient cone-membership and interiority conditions for zero duality gap and attainment in the generalized moment problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The generalized moment primal-dual pair satisfies \(\rho_{\mathrm{mom}}\leq\rho_{\mathrm{pop}}\). If \((\boldsymbol\gamma,\gamma_0)\in C(\mathbb K)\) for some \(\gamma_0\), and there exists \(\boldsymbol\lambda\in\mathbb R^{|\Gamma|}\), with \(\lambda_j\geq0\) for every \(j\in\Gamma_+\), such that \((\boldsymbol\lambda,-1)'\in\operatorname{Int}P(\mathbb K)\), then \(\rho_{\mathrm{mom}}=\rho_{\mathrm{pop}}\), and the supremum in the generalized moment problem is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak duality always bounds the moment value above by the positivity-dual value. Under the stated moment-cone membership and strict interiority condition, there is no duality gap and the generalized moment supremum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho_{\mathrm{mom}}\leq\rho_{\mathrm{pop}};\quad\text{under the additional stated assumptions, }\rho_{\mathrm{mom}}=\rho_{\mathrm{pop}}\text{ and the primal supremum is attained.}

children.title: Attainable Moment Cones
children.top_down_role: Geometry of moment vectors realizable by admissible measures.

knowledge_statements.title: Attainable Moment Cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cone of finite moment vectors represented by nonnegative measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\) be a measurable space and let \(q=(q_1,\ldots,q_d):K\to\mathbb R^d\) be measurable. Define
\[
\mathcal M_{+,q}(K):=\left\{\mu:\mu\text{ is a finite nonnegative measure on }K,\ \int_K|q_i|\,d\mu<\infty\ \text{for }i=1,\ldots,d\right\}.
\]
The attainable moment cone generated by \(q\) is
\[
C_q:=\left\{\int_Kq(x)\,d\mu(x):\mu\in\mathcal M_{+,q}(K)\right\}\subseteq\mathbb R^d.
\]
It is the convex cone of finite moment vectors represented by admissible nonnegative measures. If every Dirac measure \(\delta_x\) is admissible, then \(q(x)\in C_q\) for every \(x\in K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The attainable moment cone consists of all finite vectors of integrals of specified measurable functions against admissible finite nonnegative measures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The set \(C_q\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is a convex cone of representable moment vectors.

notation.meaning: Vector of moment-generating functions.
Finite nonnegative measures integrating every coordinate of q absolutely.
Attainable moment cone generated by q.

children.title: Closure Structure of Moment Cones
children.top_down_role: Topological closure behavior for attainable moment sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure Structure of Moment Cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closedness and bipolar characterization for finite-dimensional attainable moment cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\) be compact Hausdorff, let \(q_0=1,q_1,\ldots,q_d\in C(K)\), and let
\[
C_q:=\left\{\left(\int_Kq_0\,d\mu,\ldots,\int_Kq_d\,d\mu\right):\mu\in\mathcal M_+(K)\right\},
\]
where \(\mathcal M_+(K)\) is the cone of finite nonnegative regular Borel measures on \(K\). Then \(C_q\) is a closed convex cone. More generally, for every finite-dimensional convex cone \(C\),
\[
C^{**}=\overline C.
\]
Thus dual inequalities characterize the closure of an attainable moment cone even when the cone itself is not closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Including the mass coordinate makes the finite moment cone closed for continuous functions on a compact Hausdorff support; generally, the bidual of a finite-dimensional convex cone equals its closure.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M_+(K)\) consists of finite nonnegative regular Borel measures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cone \(C_q\) is closed, and every finite-dimensional convex cone \(C\) satisfies \(C^{**}=\overline C\).

notation.meaning: Dual cone under the Euclidean inner product.
Euclidean closure of C.
Cone of finite nonnegative regular Borel measures on K.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonclosed Moment-Cone Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete noncompact-support example where attainable moment vectors form a nonclosed cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Take \(K=\mathbb R\), \(q(x)=(x^2,x)\), and let \(C_q\) contain moments of finite nonnegative measures with finite second moment. Then
\[
C_q=\{(a,b)\in\mathbb R^2:a>0\}\cup\{(0,0)\}.
\]
Indeed, every pair with \(a>0\) is representable, whereas \(\int x^2\,d\mu=0\) forces \(\mu\) to be supported at zero and hence \(\int x\,d\mu=0\). Consequently \((1/n,1)\in C_q\) converges to \((0,1)\notin C_q\). Thus dropping compactness or an equivalent coercive normalization can destroy moment-cone closedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a noncompact support, attainable first and second moments can approach a finite vector that has no representing nonnegative measure.
assumptions_latex: Admissible measures are finite, nonnegative, and have finite second moment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The attainable cone \(C_q\) is not closed because \((1/n,1)\to(0,1)\notin C_q\).

knowledge_statements.title: Nonnegative-Function Dual Cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual of an attainable moment cone expressed by pointwise nonnegativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q=(q_1,\ldots,q_d):K\to\mathbb R^d\), suppose every Dirac measure \(\delta_x\) is admissible, and let \(C_q\) be its attainable moment cone. Then
\[
C_q^*=\left\{c\in\mathbb R^d:\langle c,y\rangle\ge0\ \text{for every }y\in C_q\right\}
=\left\{c\in\mathbb R^d:\sum_{i=1}^dc_iq_i(x)\ge0\ \text{for every }x\in K\right\}.
\]
Thus dual-cone membership is exactly pointwise nonnegativity on \(K\) of the linear combination of the moment-generating functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coefficient vector belongs to the moment cone’s dual exactly when its associated function is nonnegative everywhere on the support set.
assumptions_latex: Every \(q_i\) is measurable and integrable for admissible measures.
Every Dirac measure \(\delta_x\), \(x\in K\), is admissible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dual cone \(C_q^*\) equals the cone of coefficient vectors generating functions nonnegative on \(K\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean dual of the attainable moment cone.
Function associated with coefficient vector c.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Duality Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional conic strong duality under closedness and relative-interior feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be a closed convex cone and consider
\[
p^*=\inf\{c^\mathsf Ty:By=b,\ y\in C\},\qquad d^*=\sup\{b^\mathsf T\lambda:c-B^\mathsf T\lambda\in C^*\}.
\]
Assume the primal value is finite and there exists \(\bar y\in\operatorname{ri}C\) with \(B\bar y=b\), where relative interior is taken in \(\operatorname{span}C\). Then \(p^*=d^*\), and the dual supremum is attained. Applied to a closed attainable moment cone, this gives strong duality between its moment-coordinate program and dual positivity program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed moment-cone program with a relative-interior feasible point has no duality gap, and its dual optimum is attained.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal and dual values satisfy \(p^*=d^*\), and some dual-feasible \(\lambda^*\) attains \(d^*\).

notation.meaning: Relative interior of C in its linear span.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Attainment Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-* compactness criterion for attainment in a generalized moment problem on compact support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be compact and let \(f,a_1,\ldots,a_m\in C(K)\). Consider \[p^*=\inf_{\mu\in\mathcal M_+(K)}\left\{\int_K f\,d\mu:\int_K a_i\,d\mu=b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\right\}.\] Suppose the feasible set is nonempty and there exist \(c\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) such that \(\sum_{i=1}^m c_i a_i(x)\geq\varepsilon\) for every \(x\in K\). Then all feasible measures have uniformly bounded mass, the feasible set is weak-* compact, and some \(\mu^*\in\mathcal M_+(K)\) attains \(p^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On compact support, a positive combination of equality functions bounds feasible masses; consequently the feasible measure set is compact and the primal optimum is attained.

\(\sum_i c_i a_i\geq\varepsilon>0\) on \(K\) for some \(c\in\mathbb R^m\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Attainment Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact-superlevel criterion for attainment of the finite-dimensional moment dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K\) compact and \(f,a_1,\ldots,a_m\in C(K)\), define \[D=\left\{y\in\mathbb R^m:f(x)-\sum_{i=1}^m y_i a_i(x)\geq0\ \text{for every }x\in K\right\},\qquad d^*=\sup_{y\in D}b^\mathsf Ty.\] Suppose \(D\neq\varnothing\), \(d^*<+\infty\), and for some \(\alpha<d^*\) the superlevel set \(D_\alpha=\{y\in D:b^\mathsf Ty\geq\alpha\}\) is bounded. Because \(D_\alpha\) is closed in finite-dimensional space, it is compact; hence there exists \(y^*\in D\) satisfying \(b^\mathsf Ty^*=d^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The moment dual attains its finite supremum whenever one nonempty near-optimal superlevel set of dual multipliers is bounded.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Qualification Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Topological boundary of Slater-type qualifications for measure-conic moment formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the dual pair \(C(K)\) and \(\mathcal M(K)\), dual strict feasibility means that some \(y^0\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) satisfy \[f-\sum_{i=1}^m y_i^0a_i\geq\varepsilon\quad\text{on }K.\] This is a sufficient Slater-type qualification for standard conic strong-duality results when the primal is feasible with finite value. Its absence is not a certificate of a duality gap. Moreover, when \(K\) is infinite, the positive-measure cone has empty interior in the total-variation norm, so a primal qualification requiring norm-interior membership is unavailable; relative-interior, quasi-relative-interior, or closedness conditions must then be stated explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict dual slack is sufficient but not necessary; on infinite support, ordinary norm-interior primal Slater conditions are generally unavailable.
assumptions_latex: The moment problem is posed over the dual pair \(C(K),\mathcal M(K)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{int}_{\|\cdot\|_{TV}}\mathcal M_+(K)=\varnothing\), while failure of dual strict feasibility alone does not imply \(p^*>d^*\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a primal minimization moment problem with value \(p^*\) and its dual maximization problem with value \(d^*\), weak duality gives \(d^*\leq p^*\). The pair has a positive duality gap when both values are finite and \[g:=p^*-d^*>0.\] This property concerns optimal values only: it neither asserts nor excludes attainment on either side. Cases involving \(p^*=+\infty\) or \(d^*=-\infty\) are infeasibility or unbounded-value regimes and are not finite positive duality gaps under this definition.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap–Nonattainment Interactions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical separation of value equality from primal and dual attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite values satisfying weak duality, introduce the predicates \(G_0\!:\ p^*=d^*\), \(A_P\!:\ p^*\text{ is attained}\), and \(A_D\!:\ d^*\text{ is attained}\). Strong duality is the value predicate \(G_0\) and does not, by definition, include either attainment predicate. Thus \(G_0\), \(A_P\), and \(A_D\) must be reported separately. In particular, failure of \(A_P\) or \(A_D\) does not logically establish \(p^*>d^*\), while a positive gap does not by itself identify which side, if either, fails to attain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero gap, primal attainment, and dual attainment are distinct predicates; none should be inferred solely from failure of another.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_0\), \(A_P\), and \(A_D\) are separate status predicates.

knowledge_statements.title: Carathéodory–Tchakaloff Reduction Principles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite atomic representation preserving a finite-dimensional continuous function space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be compact, let \(V\subseteq C(K)\) be a finite-dimensional real vector space containing the constant function, and let \(\mu\in\mathcal M_+(K)\). If \(r=\dim V\), then there exist points \(x_1,\ldots,x_s\in K\) and weights \(w_1,\ldots,w_s>0\), with \(s\leq r\), such that the atomic measure \(\nu=\sum_{j=1}^s w_j\delta_{x_j}\) satisfies \[\int_K v\,d\nu=\int_K v\,d\mu\qquad\text{for every }v\in V.\] Thus every finite collection of prescribed continuous moments has a positive atomic representative using at most the dimension of its function span.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any positive measure can be replaced, for finitely many continuous moments, by a positive atomic measure with at most the span dimension many atoms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\nu=\sum_{j=1}^s w_j\delta_{x_j}\) with \(s\leq\dim V\) and \(\int v\,d\nu=\int v\,d\mu\) for all \(v\in V\).

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Support Model Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Atom-count bound for preserving constraints and objective in a moment model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a generalized moment model on compact \(K\) with continuous constraint functions \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\), objective \(f\), and a feasible finite positive measure \(\mu\). Set \[V=\operatorname{span}\{1,a_1,\ldots,a_m,f\},\qquad r=\dim V.\] There exists a positive atomic measure \(
u\) supported on at most \(r\leq m+2\) points such that \(\int a_i\,d
u=\int a_i\,d\mu\) for every \(i\), \(
u(K)=\mu(K)\), and \(\int f\,d
u=\int f\,d\mu\). Consequently, whenever the primal optimum is attained, an optimal atomic measure exists with at most \(r\) atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Preserving mass, m constraints, and the objective requires at most the dimension of their function span, hence at most m+2 atoms.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\operatorname{supp}\nu|\leq r=\dim\operatorname{span}\{1,a_1,\ldots,a_m,f\}\leq m+2\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Localizing-Matrix Criteria for the Compact K-Moment Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representability of an infinite multisequence on a compact basic semialgebraic set, including the reduced criterion under the stated SOS compactness hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\mathbb K=\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(\mathbf x)\ge0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}$ be compact, let $g_0=1$, and let $\mathbf y=(y_{\boldsymbol\alpha})_{\boldsymbol\alpha\in\mathbb N^n}$. Then $\mathbf y$ has a finite Borel representing measure supported on $\mathbb K$ if and only if $L_{\mathbf y}(f^2g_J)\ge0$ for every $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}$ and every $f\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]$; equivalently, $\mathbf M_r(g_J\mathbf y)\succeq0$ for every such $J$ and every $r\in\mathbb N$. If, additionally, $u=u_0+\sum_{i=1}^m u_i g_i$ with $u_i\in\Sigma[\mathbf x]$ for $i=0,\ldots,m$ and $\{\mathbf x:u(\mathbf x)\ge0\}$ compact, these conditions are equivalent to testing only $g_j$, $j=0,\ldots,m$: $L_{\mathbf y}(f^2g_j)\ge0$ for every $f$, or equivalently $\mathbf M_r(g_j\mathbf y)\succeq0$ for every $r$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact basic semialgebraic set, a sequence has a finite supported representing measure exactly when all localizing matrices associated with products of defining inequalities are positive semidefinite. Under the additional SOS compactness condition, it suffices to test the individual defining polynomials and the constant polynomial.
assumptions_latex: \mathbb K=\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(\mathbf x)\ge0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\text{ is compact}
\mathbf y=(y_{\boldsymbol\alpha})_{\boldsymbol\alpha\in\mathbb N^n},\quad L_{\mathbf y}:\mathbb R[\mathbf x]\to\mathbb R
\text{For the reduced criterion: }u=u_0+\sum_{i=1}^m u_i g_i,\quad u_i\in\Sigma[\mathbf x],\quad \{\mathbf x:u(\mathbf x)\ge0\}\text{ is compact}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbf y\text{ has a finite Borel }\mathbb K\text{-representing measure}\iff \forall J,f,\ L_{\mathbf y}(f^2g_J)\ge0\iff \forall J,r,\ \mathbf M_r(g_J\mathbf y)\succeq0,\text{ with the reduced }j=0,\ldots,m\text{ tests under the additional hypothesis}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: The Real K-Moment Problem and Localizing Matrices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Foundational definitions for infinite moment sequences over a basic semialgebraic support set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given $g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]$, define $\mathbb K:=\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(\mathbf x)\ge 0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}$ and $g_0:=1$. For $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}$, let $g_J:=\prod_{j\in J}g_j$, with $g_\varnothing:=1$. The real $\mathbb K$-moment problem asks which infinite sequences $\mathbf y=(y_{\boldsymbol\alpha})_{\boldsymbol\alpha\in\mathbb N^n}$ are moment sequences of measures supported on $\mathbb K$. For $r\in\mathbb N$, $\mathbf M_r(g_J\mathbf y)$ is the corresponding localizing matrix; for $J=\varnothing$, it is the moment matrix $\mathbf M_r(\mathbf y)$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The real K-moment problem characterizes infinite sequences that are moments of measures supported on a basic semialgebraic set. Products of its defining polynomials yield localizing matrices, and the empty product yields the ordinary moment matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Full Moment Sequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full multivariate moment sequence and its representing measure on a prescribed set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). A full real sequence is a family \(y=(y_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n}\) indexed by every multi-index. It is a full \(K\)-moment sequence if there exists a positive Borel measure \(\mu\) supported on \(K\), with every monomial integrable, such that \[y_\alpha=\int_K x^\alpha\,d\mu(x)\qquad\text{for all }\alpha\in\mathbb N^n.\] Such a measure is called a representing measure for \(y\). The definition prescribes moments of all degrees and does not assert that the representing measure is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full K-moment sequence records every monomial moment of a positive measure supported on K, across all multi-index degrees.
assumptions_latex: Every monomial \(x^\alpha\) is integrable with respect to the representing measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_\alpha=\int_Kx^\alpha\,d\mu\) for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb N^n\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every polynomial \(p(x)=\sum_{\alpha}p_\alpha x^\alpha\) with finitely many nonzero coefficients, define \[L_y(p):=\sum_\alpha p_\alpha y_\alpha.\] This defines the unique linear functional \(L_y:\mathbb R[x]\to\mathbb R\) such that \(L_y(x^\alpha)=y_\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb N^n\). If a positive Borel measure \(\mu\) supported on \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) represents \(y\), meaning \(y_\alpha=\int_Kx^\alpha\,d\mu(x)\), then \[L_y(p)=\int_Kp(x)\,d\mu(x)\qquad\text{for every }p\in\mathbb R[x].\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The moment sequence determines a unique linear functional by coefficient pairing; whenever the sequence has a representing measure, evaluating the functional equals integrating the polynomial against that measure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Riesz Functional, Representing Measure, and Polynomial Multiplication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the Riesz functional of a real multisequence, representing positive Borel measures, and polynomial multiplication of sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a real sequence \(\boldsymbol\phi=(\phi_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n}\), define its Riesz linear functional by \(L_{\boldsymbol\phi}(p)=\sum_\alpha p_\alpha\phi_\alpha\) for \(p=\sum_\alpha p_\alpha\mathbf x^\alpha\). The sequence has a representing positive Borel measure \(\mu\) on \(\mathbb R^n\) if \(\phi_\alpha=\int_{\mathbb R^n}\mathbf x^\alpha\,d\mu\) for every \(\alpha\), in which case \(L_{\boldsymbol\phi}(p)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}p\,d\mu\). For \(g=\sum_\gamma g_\gamma\mathbf x^\gamma\), define \((g\boldsymbol\phi)_\alpha=\sum_\gamma g_\gamma\phi_{\alpha+\gamma}\); then \(L_{g\boldsymbol\phi}(p)=L_{\boldsymbol\phi}(gp)\) for every \(p\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A real multisequence defines a Riesz functional by coefficient pairing. It has a representing positive Borel measure when its entries are the measure's moments. Polynomial multiplication produces a shifted sequence whose functional applies the original functional to the polynomial product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_{\boldsymbol\phi}(p)=\sum_\alpha p_\alpha\phi_\alpha,\qquad \phi_\alpha=\int \mathbf x^\alpha\,d\mu\ \forall\alpha\Rightarrow L_{\boldsymbol\phi}(p)=\int p\,d\mu,\qquad L_{g\boldsymbol\phi}(p)=L_{\boldsymbol\phi}(gp).

children.top_down_role: Matrix representations encoding positivity, inequalities, equalities, and truncation structure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Moment-matrix SDP relaxation of polynomial optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records the moment/localizing-matrix lifting and the resulting order-k SDP relaxation without asserting the subsequent convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v_k(x)\) denote the monomial vector used at order \(k\), including the constant monomial, and define \(M_k(x)=v_k(x)v_k(x)^\top\succeq0\), with \(M_0(x)=[1]\). For a constraint polynomial \(f_i\), define the pointwise localizing matrix \(M_{i,k-1}(x)=f_i(x)M_{k-1}(x)\). Replacing each monomial \(x^\alpha\) occurring in the objective and matrix entries by an independent variable \(y_\alpha\) makes the objective linear and each matrix constraint affine in \(y\). Every feasible point \(x\) of \(P\) lifts via \(y_\alpha=x^\alpha\) to a feasible point of this SDP, so the resulting order-\(k\) problem is a relaxation of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Moment matrices are outer products of monomial vectors, and multiplying them by constraint polynomials gives localizing matrices. Replacing monomials by independent moment variables produces linear matrix inequalities and hence an SDP relaxation of the polynomial problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\alpha\mapsto y_\alpha\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \text{an order-}k\text{ semidefinite relaxation of }P

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The order-\(d\) truncated moment matrix of \(y\) is the symmetric matrix indexed by \(\mathbb N_d^n:=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n:|\alpha|\le d\}\) and defined by \[[M_d(y)]_{\alpha,\beta}:=y_{\alpha+\beta}.\] Equivalently, \(M_d(y)=L_y(v_dv_d^{\mathsf T})\), with \(L_y\) applied entrywise. Consequently, for \(p(x)=\sum_{|\alpha|\le d}c_\alpha x^\alpha\), \[c^{\mathsf T}M_d(y)c=L_y(p^2).\] If \(y\) has a positive representing measure, then \(M_d(y)\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A truncated moment matrix is the Hankel-type matrix whose alpha-beta entry is the moment indexed by their sum; its quadratic form evaluates the Riesz functional on a polynomial square.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At truncation order \(2d+\deg h\), the equality-localizing condition for \(h(x)=0\) is \[L_y(hp)=0\qquad\text{for every }p\in\mathbb R[x]_{2d}.\] In monomial coordinates this is the family of linear equations \[\sum_\gamma h_\gamma y_{\alpha+\gamma}=0\qquad(|\alpha|\le2d).\] Equivalently, every fully defined entry of the localizing matrix for \(h\) vanishes. Any positive measure representing \(y\) and supported on \(\{x:h(x)=0\}\) satisfies these relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equality constraint forces every available moment of h times a test polynomial to vanish, equivalently producing linear shifted-moment equations or a zero localizing matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Ideal-Based Localizing Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generator-independent equality relations from a truncated polynomial ideal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_s\rangle\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\), and let \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le D}\) define \(L_y\) on \(\mathbb R[x]_D\). The degree-\(D\) ideal-localizing condition is \[L_y(q)=0\qquad\text{for every }q\in I\cap\mathbb R[x]_D.\] This condition depends only on the truncated ideal subspace \(I\cap\mathbb R[x]_D\), not on a selected generating family. Any positive measure representing \(y\) through degree \(D\) and supported on the real variety \(V_{\mathbb R}(I)\) necessarily satisfies these relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At degree D, the truncated Riesz functional must annihilate every ideal polynomial of degree at most D. This condition is independent of the chosen generators, and it is necessary for a representing measure supported on the ideal's real variety.
assumptions_latex: \(I=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_s\rangle\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\) is a polynomial ideal.
\(D\in\mathbb N\), and \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le D}\) is a real truncated sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_y(q)=0\) for every \(q\in I\cap\mathbb R[x]_D\) is the generator-independent ideal-localizing condition at degree \(D\).

notation.meaning: Ideal generated by the equality polynomials.
Subspace of ideal polynomials having total degree at most D.
Truncated Riesz functional defined by the moments through degree D.

knowledge_statements.title: Quotient-Ring Moment Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment functional and bilinear form after quotienting by equality relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\) be an ideal, let \(L:\mathbb R[x]\to\mathbb R\) be linear, and suppose \(L(q)=0\) for every \(q\in I\). There is a unique linear functional \(\bar L:\mathbb R[x]/I\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \[\bar L([p])=L(p)\qquad\text{for every }p\in\mathbb R[x].\] Equivalently, \(L=\bar L\circ\pi\), where \(\pi(p)=[p]\). The induced quotient moment form is \[B_{\bar L}([p],[q]):=\bar L([pq])\qquad([p],[q]\in\mathbb R[x]/I).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear functional that annihilates an ideal descends uniquely to the quotient ring, where multiplication of residue classes induces the corresponding moment bilinear form.
assumptions_latex: \(L:\mathbb R[x]\to\mathbb R\) is linear and satisfies \(L(q)=0\) for every \(q\in I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is a unique linear functional \(\bar L:\mathbb R[x]/I\to\mathbb R\) with \(\bar L([p])=L(p)\), and the induced moment form is \(B_{\bar L}([p],[q])=\bar L([pq])\).

notation.meaning: Residue class of p modulo I.
Functional induced on the quotient ring.
Canonical quotient map from the polynomial ring to its quotient by I.

knowledge_statements.title: Monomial Polynomial Bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard total-degree monomial basis for multivariate polynomials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\ge1\) and \(d\in\mathbb N\). For \(\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n)\in\mathbb N^n\), set \(x^\alpha:=x_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots x_n^{\alpha_n}\) and \(|\alpha|:=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i\). The total-degree monomial basis of \(\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]_d\) is \[\mathcal M_d:=\{x^\alpha:\alpha\in\mathbb N^n,\ |\alpha|\le d\}.\] Every \(p\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]_d\) has a unique expansion \[p(x)=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb N_d^n}p_\alpha x^\alpha,\] and \(|\mathcal M_d|=\binom{n+d}{d}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For n variables, the monomials of total degree at most d form a basis of the degree-at-most-d polynomial space, yielding unique coefficients and dimension binomial(n+d,d).
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb N\) with \(n\ge1\), \(d\in\mathbb N\), and the coefficient field is \(\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x^\alpha:|\alpha|\le d\}\) is a basis of \(\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]_d\), so every polynomial in that space has unique monomial coefficients.

notation.meaning: Multi-index monomial.
Multi-indices of total degree at most d.
Total-degree monomial basis through degree d.

children.top_down_role: Nonmonomial coordinate systems for moment representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Alternative Polynomial Bases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invertible basis changes for finite-degree moment matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\ge1\), \(d\in\mathbb N\), \(N=\binom{n+d}{d}\), and let \(y=(y_\gamma)_{|\gamma|\le2d}\) define \(L_y\) on \(\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]_{2d}\). If \(b_d=(b_1,\ldots,b_N)^{\mathsf T}\) and \(v_d\) are ordered bases of \(\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]_d\), then there is a unique invertible matrix \(T\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}\) such that \(b_d(x)=Tv_d(x)\). Defining \[M_{b_d}(y):=L_y(b_db_d^{\mathsf T})\] entrywise gives \[M_{b_d}(y)=T M_d(y)T^{\mathsf T}.\] Consequently, positive semidefiniteness and rank are invariant under this basis change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For moment data through degree 2d, any ordered basis of degree-at-most-d polynomials is an invertible transformation of the monomial basis, and its moment matrix is the corresponding congruence transformation.
assumptions_latex: \(n\ge1\), \(d\in\mathbb N\), and \(y=(y_\gamma)_{|\gamma|\le2d}\) is a real truncated sequence.
\(b_d=(b_1,\ldots,b_N)^{\mathsf T}\) and \(v_d\) are ordered bases of \(\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]_d\), where \(N=\binom{n+d}{d}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is a unique invertible \(T\) with \(b_d=Tv_d\), and \(M_{b_d}(y)=TM_d(y)T^{\mathsf T}\).

notation.meaning: Alternative ordered polynomial basis vector.
Ordered monomial basis vector.
Invertible change-of-basis matrix from the monomial basis.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite moment index set is a set \(B\subseteq\mathbb N^n\) specifying the available coordinates \(y_B=(y_\gamma)_{\gamma\in B}\). For a polynomial basis supported on \(A\subseteq\mathbb N^n\), every product \(x^\alpha x^\beta\) has exponent \(\alpha+\beta\); therefore its moment Gram matrix is defined whenever \[A+A:=\{\alpha+\beta:\alpha,\beta\in A\}\subseteq B.\] For the total-degree set \(A=\mathbb N_d^n\), one has \(A+A=\mathbb N_{2d}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A moment index set records available moments. A basis indexed by A requires all sum indices in A+A; total-degree d bases therefore require moments through degree 2d.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis–Index Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact condition for constructing a moment Gram matrix from truncated data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\subseteq\mathbb N^n\) be finite, let \(y_B=(y_\gamma)_{\gamma\in B}\), and define \(L_{y_B}(\sum_{\gamma\in B}p_\gamma x^\gamma):=\sum_{\gamma\in B}p_\gamma y_\gamma\) on \(\mathbb R[x]_B:=\operatorname{span}\{x^\gamma:\gamma\in B\}\). For a finite ordered polynomial family \(b=(b_1,\ldots,b_N)^{\mathsf T}\), the pair \((b,B)\) is moment-compatible if and only if \[\operatorname{supp}(b_i b_j)\subseteq B\qquad(1\le i,j\le N).\] Under this condition every entry \[[M_b(y_B)]_{ij}:=L_{y_B}(b_i b_j)\] is defined by the available moments. If \(A:=\bigcup_{i=1}^N\operatorname{supp}(b_i)\), then \(A+A\subseteq B\) is a sufficient compatibility test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite polynomial family and a moment index set are compatible exactly when every exponent occurring in every pairwise product is available, so each moment Gram-matrix entry can be evaluated from the truncated data.
assumptions_latex: \(B\subseteq\mathbb N^n\) is finite, and \(y_B=(y_\gamma)_{\gamma\in B}\) is the available moment data.
\(b=(b_1,\ldots,b_N)^{\mathsf T}\) is a finite ordered family in \(\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair \((b,B)\) is moment-compatible exactly when \(\operatorname{supp}(b_i b_j)\subseteq B\) for every \(i,j\).

notation.meaning: Exponent support of a polynomial.
Available moment index set.
Coefficient-pairing functional on polynomials supported in B.
Moment Gram matrix of the family b computed from y_B.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: PSD criteria for truncated Stieltjes and Hamburger moment vectors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes finite univariate moment data on the nonnegative half-line and the real line.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb N_0\), set \(M_0=1\), and define \(H_n=(M_{i+j})_{i,j=0}^n\) and \(H_n^{(1)}=(M_{i+j+1})_{i,j=0}^n\). Then \((M_1,\ldots,M_{2n+1})\) is a feasible \((1,2n+1,[0,\infty))\)-moment vector if and only if \(H_n\succeq0\) and \(H_n^{(1)}\succeq0\). Moreover, \((M_1,\ldots,M_{2n})\) is a feasible \((1,2n,\mathbb R)\)-moment vector if and only if \(H_n\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Odd-order moment data on the nonnegative half-line are feasible exactly when both the ordinary and shifted Hankel moment matrices are positive semidefinite. Even-order moment data on the real line are feasible exactly when the ordinary Hankel moment matrix is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (M_1,\ldots,M_{2n+1})\in\mathcal M(1,2n+1,[0,\infty))\iff H_n\succeq0\ \land\ H_n^{(1)}\succeq0;\qquad (M_1,\ldots,M_{2n})\in\mathcal M(1,2n,\mathbb R)\iff H_n\succeq0.

knowledge_statements.title: Hausdorff Moment Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical characterization of moment sequences supported on the unit interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(y=(y_n)_{n\ge 0}\) be a real sequence and define \(\Delta y_n=y_{n+1}-y_n\). There exists a finite positive Borel measure \(\mu\) on \([0,1]\) satisfying \(y_n=\int_0^1 t^n\,d\mu(t)\) for every \(n\ge 0\) if and only if
\[
(-1)^k\Delta^k y_n\ge 0\qquad(n,k\in\mathbb N).
\]
When it exists, the representing measure is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequence is represented by a unique positive measure on the unit interval exactly when all its alternating finite differences are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_n=\int_0^1t^n\,d\mu(t)\) for a unique finite positive Borel measure \(\mu\) if and only if \((-1)^k\Delta^ky_n\ge0\) for all \(n,k\).

notation.meaning: Forward-difference operator, \(\Delta y_n=y_{n+1}-y_n\).
Finite positive Borel measure on the unit interval.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full and truncated supported moment problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representability of complete or finitely indexed multivariate moment data on a basic closed semialgebraic set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]$ and $K=\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(\mathbf x)\geq0, j=1,\ldots,m\}$. The full $K$-moment problem asks whether an infinite real sequence $\mathbf y=(y_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n}$ admits a finite Borel measure $\mu$ supported on $K$ such that $y_\alpha=\int_K\mathbf x^\alpha\,d\mu$ for every $\alpha\in\mathbb N^n$. Given a finite set $\Delta\subset\mathbb N^n$, the truncated $K$-moment problem asks whether data $(y_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\Delta}$ admit a measure $\mu$ supported on $K$ satisfying these identities for every $\alpha\in\Delta$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full supported moment problem asks whether an entire infinite sequence consists of moments of a finite Borel measure supported on K. The truncated problem asks the analogous question for finitely many prescribed moments.
assumptions_latex: For the truncated problem, $\Delta\subset\mathbb N^n$ is finite
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbf y\text{ solves the full }K\text{-moment problem}\iff \exists\text{ finite Borel }\mu\text{ supported on }K:\ y_\alpha=\int_K\mathbf x^\alpha d\mu\ \forall\alpha\in\mathbb N^n;\quad \mathbf y\text{ solves the truncated problem}\iff \exists\mu\text{ supported on }K:\ y_\alpha=\int_K\mathbf x^\alpha d\mu\ \forall\alpha\in\Delta.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasible supported truncated moment vector
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines multivariate moment data representable by a random vector supported on a prescribed subset of Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\in\mathbb N\), \(k\in\mathbb N_0\), \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and \(\sigma=(\sigma_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le k}\). The vector \(\sigma\) is a feasible \((n,k,\Omega)\)-moment vector if there exists a random vector \(X=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)\) taking values in \(\Omega\) such that \(\sigma_\alpha=\mathbb E[X^\alpha]=\mathbb E[X_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots X_n^{\alpha_n}]\) for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n\) with \(|\alpha|\le k\). Any such \(X\) has a \(\sigma\)-feasible distribution, denoted \(X\sim\sigma\), and the set of feasible vectors is denoted \(\mathcal M(n,k,\Omega)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A truncated multivariate moment vector is feasible on Ω when its entries through total degree k are the moments of a random vector taking values in Ω. Such a distribution is called σ-feasible, and all feasible vectors form M(n,k,Ω).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sigma\in\mathcal M(n,k,\Omega)\iff \exists X:\ \mathbb P(X\in\Omega)=1\ \text{and}\ \sigma_\alpha=\mathbb E[X^\alpha]\ \forall\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n\ \text{with}\ |\alpha|\le k.

knowledge_statements.title: Full Multivariate Moment Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full moment representability on a prescribed closed support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and let \(y=(y_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n}\) be a full real multisequence. The full \(K\)-moment problem asks whether there exists a positive Borel measure \(\mu\) supported on \(K\), with every monomial integrable, such that
\[
y_\alpha=\int_K x^\alpha\,d\mu(x)\qquad(\alpha\in\mathbb N^n).
\]
Such a measure is called a \(K\)-representing measure for \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full multivariate moment problem asks whether every entry of an infinite multisequence is the corresponding monomial moment of one positive measure supported on a prescribed set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The problem is feasible exactly when a positive Borel measure \(\mu\) supported on \(K\) satisfies \(y_\alpha=\int_Kx^\alpha\,d\mu\) for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb N^n\).

notation.meaning: Monomial \(x_1^{\alpha_1}\cdots x_n^{\alpha_n}\).
Full multisequence indexed by all multi-indices.

knowledge_statements.title: Truncated K-Moment Problem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree-bounded multivariate moment representability on a prescribed support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(d\in\mathbb N\), a closed set \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and real data \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le 2d}\). The truncated \(K\)-moment problem asks whether there exists a positive Borel measure \(\mu\) supported on \(K\) such that
\[
y_\alpha=\int_Kx^\alpha\,d\mu(x)
\qquad\text{for every }|\alpha|\le2d.
\]
Any such \(\mu\) is a representing measure for the truncated sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The truncated K-moment problem asks whether finitely many prescribed moments through degree 2d come from a positive measure supported on K.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility means that some positive Borel measure \(\mu\) supported on \(K\) realizes every specified moment.

notation.meaning: Multi-indices \(\alpha\) satisfying \(|\alpha|\le2d\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual-cone extension criterion for truncated K-moments
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes degree-2d K-moment sequences by the existence of a degree-2d+2 dual-cone extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and \(d\in\mathbb N\). A sequence
\[
y=(y_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb N_{2d}^n}
\]
has a representing measure supported on \(K\) if and only if it has an extension
\[
\widetilde y=(\widetilde y_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb N_{2d+2}^n}\in C_{2d+2}(K)^*
\]
satisfying \(\widetilde y_\alpha=y_\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb N_{2d}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For closed K, degree-2d data are K-moment data exactly when they extend through degree 2d+2 to a functional nonnegative on all degree-2d+2 polynomials nonnegative on K.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y\text{ has a representing measure supported on }K\iff\exists\widetilde y\in C_{2d+2}(K)^*\text{ extending }y.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Representability of the odd-degree restriction of a dual-cone sequence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A truncated representability theorem for an arbitrary closed support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and let \(d\geq1\). If
\[
y=(y_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb N_{2d}^n}\in C_{2d}(K)^*,
\]
then the restriction \((y_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb N_{2d-1}^n}\) has a representing measure supported on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For closed K, a degree-2d functional nonnegative on every degree-2d polynomial nonnegative on K becomes representable by a measure on K when restricted to degrees at most 2d−1.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\mu\geq0\text{ supported on }K\text{ such that }y_\alpha=\int_Kx^\alpha\,d\mu\quad\forall\alpha\in\mathbb N_{2d-1}^n.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual cone of nonnegative polynomials and truncated K-moments
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines degree-bounded nonnegative-polynomial duality and its connection with moment sequences supported on a prescribed set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(d\in\mathbb N\), define
\[
C_d(K)=\{g\in\mathbb R[x]_d:g(x)\geq0\ \forall x\in K\}.
\]
Its dual cone is
\[
C_d(K)^*=\{y=(y_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb N_d^n}:L_y(g)\geq0\ \forall g\in C_d(K)\}.
\]
Every degree-\(d\) moment sequence of a positive measure supported on \(K\) belongs to \(C_d(K)^*\). If \(K\) is compact, every element of \(C_d(K)^*\) has such a representing measure. The truncated \(K\)-moment problem asks which finite sequences have representing measures supported on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Moment sequences of positive measures supported on K lie in the dual cone of degree-at-most-d polynomials nonnegative on K. For compact K, this inclusion is equality. The truncated K-moment problem characterizes such representable finite sequences.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{y:\exists\mu\geq0,\ y_\alpha=\int_Kx^\alpha\,d\mu\ \forall\alpha\in\mathbb N_d^n\}\subseteq C_d(K)^*,\qquad K\text{ compact}\Longrightarrow\text{equality}.

knowledge_statements.title: Riesz–Haviland Theorem Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-sequence representability criterion for a closed support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and let \(y=(y_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n}\). Define the Riesz functional by \(L_y(\sum_\alpha p_\alpha x^\alpha)=\sum_\alpha p_\alpha y_\alpha\). Then \(y\) has a positive Borel representing measure supported on \(K\) if and only if
\[
L_y(p)\ge0
\quad\text{for every }p\in\mathbb R[x]\text{ satisfying }p(x)\ge0\text{ on }K.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full multisequence has a K-supported representing measure exactly when its Riesz functional is nonnegative on every polynomial nonnegative on K.
assumptions_latex: \(y\) is indexed by all of \(\mathbb N^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\) is \(K\)-representable if and only if \(L_y\) is nonnegative on every polynomial nonnegative on \(K\).

notation.meaning: Riesz functional induced by the full moment sequence.
Cone of polynomials nonnegative on K.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive Extension Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representability characterized by extension of a truncated Riesz functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed, let \(E\subseteq\mathbb R[x]\) be a finite-dimensional linear subspace containing \(1\), and let \(L:E\to\mathbb R\) be linear. A positive Borel measure \(\mu\) supported on \(K\) with \(L(p)=\int_Kp\,d\mu\) for every \(p\in E\) exists if and only if \(L\) extends to a linear functional \(\widetilde L:\mathbb R[x]\to\mathbb R\) satisfying
\[
\widetilde L(p)\ge0
\quad\text{whenever }p\ge0\text{ on }K.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Truncated data have a K-supported representing measure exactly when their functional extends to all polynomials while remaining positive on every polynomial nonnegative on K.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A \(K\)-representing measure for \(L\) exists if and only if a \(K\)-positive extension \(\widetilde L\) exists.

notation.meaning: Polynomial subspace on which moment data are prescribed.
Extension of L to the full polynomial ring.

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Sensitive Representability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonicity and exact support interpretation of moment representability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a closed set \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), write \(\mathcal M(K)\) for the full sequences admitting a positive Borel representing measure supported on \(K\). If \(K_1\subseteq K_2\), then
\[
\mathcal M(K_1)\subseteq\mathcal M(K_2).
\]
Moreover, if \(y\) has a unique representing measure \(\mu\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), then for every closed \(K\),
\[
y\in\mathcal M(K)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{supp}\mu\subseteq K.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allowing a larger support can only enlarge the representable moment cone; for a determinate sequence, K-representability is exactly containment of its unique measure's support in K.
assumptions_latex: For the equivalence, \(y\) has a unique representing measure \(\mu\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal M(K_1)\subseteq\mathcal M(K_2)\), and determinacy gives \(y\in\mathcal M(K)\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{supp}\mu\subseteq K\).

notation.meaning: Cone of full moment sequences representable on K.
Closed support of the representing measure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Carleman sufficient condition for bounded-density moment representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Provides a sufficient, not necessary, criterion for bounded-density representability on the noncompact domain \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbf z\) be the moment sequence of a finite Borel measure \(\mu\) on \(\mathbb R^n\) satisfying the generalized Carleman condition \[\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}L_{\mathbf z}(x_i^{2k})^{-1/(2k)}=\infty\qquad\forall i=1,\ldots,n.\] If there exists \(\kappa>0\) such that \[0\le L_{\mathbf y}(f^2)\le\kappa L_{\mathbf z}(f^2)\qquad\forall f\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x],\] then \(\mathbf y\) has a finite Borel representing measure \(\nu\) on \(\mathbb R^n\) with bounded density relative to \(\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the reference measure satisfies the coordinatewise generalized Carleman condition and the candidate moment functional is nonnegative and uniformly dominated by the reference functional on every polynomial square, then the candidate sequence has a finite representing measure with bounded density relative to the reference measure.
assumptions_latex: \mathbf z\text{ is the moment sequence of a finite Borel measure }\mu\text{ on }\mathbb R^n
\exists\kappa>0:\ 0\le L_{\mathbf y}(f^2)\le\kappa L_{\mathbf z}(f^2)\quad\forall f\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ a finite Borel representing measure }\nu\text{ for }\mathbf y\text{ on }\mathbb R^n\text{ having bounded density relative to }\mu.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded-density moment representation relative to a reference measure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a moment representation whose representing measure has a nonnegative essentially bounded density with respect to a fixed finite reference measure, and distinguishes absolute continuity from measure domination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mu\) be a finite Borel measure on \(\mathbb K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). A sequence \(\mathbf y=(y_{ oldsymbol\alpha})_{ oldsymbol\alpha\in\mathbb N^n}\) has a bounded-density representation relative to \(\mu\) if there exists \(0\le h\in L_\infty(\mathbb K,\mu)\) such that \[y_{ oldsymbol\alpha}=\int_{\mathbb K}\mathbf x^{ oldsymbol\alpha}h\,d\mu\qquad orall oldsymbol\alpha\in\mathbb N^n.\] Writing \(d
u=h\,d\mu\), one has \(
u\ll\mu\), and \(h=d
u/d\mu\). For finite measures on a common \(\sigma\)-algebra, \(
u\le\mu\) means \(
u(B)\le\mu(B)\) for every measurable \(B\); this domination implies \(
u\ll\mu\), whereas the converse need not hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded-density moment representation expresses every moment using a nonnegative essentially bounded density relative to a fixed finite reference measure. The induced measure is absolutely continuous with respect to the reference measure. Measure domination implies absolute continuity, but absolute continuity alone does not imply domination.
assumptions_latex: \mu\text{ is a finite Borel measure on }\mathbb K\subseteq\mathbb R^n
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\exists h\in L_\infty(\mathbb K,\mu),\ h\ge0:\ y_{ oldsymbol\alpha}=\int_{\mathbb K}\mathbf x^{ oldsymbol\alpha}h\,d\mu\  orall oldsymbol\alpha;\quad d
u=h\,d\mu\Rightarrow
u\ll\mu;\quad 
u\le\mu\Rightarrow
u\ll\mu	ext{, but not conversely.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compact semialgebraic criteria for bounded-density moment representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes bounded-density representability on a compact basic semialgebraic set through domination of moment functionals, including quadratic-module and normalized-generator reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbb K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) be compact, let \(g_J:=\prod_{j\in J}g_j\), and let \(\mathbf z\) be the moment sequence of a finite Borel measure \(\mu\) on \(\mathbb K\). A sequence \(\mathbf y\) has a finite Borel representing measure on \(\mathbb K\) with bounded density relative to \(\mu\) if and only if there exists a scalar \(\kappa\) such that \[0\le L_{\mathbf y}(f^2g_J)\le\kappa L_{\mathbf z}(f^2g_J)\qquad\forall f\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x],\ \forall J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}.\] If \(N-\|\mathbf x\|^2\in Q(g)\), this condition may be replaced by \[0\le L_{\mathbf y}(f^2g_j)\le\kappa L_{\mathbf z}(f^2g_j)\qquad\forall f\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x],\ j=0,\ldots,m,\] where \(g_0=1\). If instead \(0\le g_j\le1\) on \(\mathbb K\) and \(1,g_1,\ldots,g_m\) generate \(\mathbb R[\mathbf x]\), bounded-density representability is equivalent to the existence of \(\kappa\) such that \[0\le L_{\mathbf y}\!\left(g^{\boldsymbol\alpha}(1-g)^{\boldsymbol\beta}\right)\le\kappa L_{\mathbf z}\!\left(g^{\boldsymbol\alpha}(1-g)^{\boldsymbol\beta}\right)\qquad\forall\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta\in\mathbb N^m.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact basic semialgebraic set, bounded-density moment representability is equivalent to uniform domination of the candidate moment functional by the reference moment functional on the stated positive polynomial tests. Additional quadratic-module or normalized-generator assumptions permit the corresponding reduced test families.
assumptions_latex: \mathbf z\text{ is the moment sequence of a finite Borel measure }\mu\text{ on }\mathbb K
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbf y\text{ has a finite representing measure with bounded density relative to }\mu\iff\exists\kappa:\ 0\le L_{\mathbf y}(f^2g_J)\le\kappa L_{\mathbf z}(f^2g_J)\ \forall f,J,\text{ with the stated conditional reductions.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Representing measures and determinacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Terminology for measures representing full or truncated moment data and for uniqueness or nonuniqueness of representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For full or truncated moment data $\mathbf y$, a measure $\mu$ is a representing measure if it satisfies $y_\alpha=\int_K\mathbf x^\alpha\,d\mu$ for every prescribed index $\alpha$. A representing measure, and equivalently the corresponding moment data, is called determinate when it is the unique representing measure and indeterminate otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A representing measure reproduces every prescribed moment. The representation is determinate when that measure is unique and indeterminate when more than one representing measure exists.
assumptions_latex: $\mathbf y$ is full or truncated moment data
$\mu$ is a measure supported on the prescribed set $K$
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mu\text{ represents }\mathbf y\iff y_\alpha=\int_K\mathbf x^\alpha d\mu\text{ for every prescribed }\alpha;\qquad \mathbf y\text{ is determinate}\iff \mu\text{ is its unique representing measure}.

knowledge_statements.title: Moment-Determinate Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness of a representing measure relative to a support class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and let \(y\) be a full sequence having at least one positive Borel representing measure supported on \(K\). The sequence \(y\) is \(K\)-determinate if any two positive Borel measures \(\mu\) and \(\nu\) supported on \(K\) that satisfy
\[
\int_Kx^\alpha\,d\mu=
\int_Kx^\alpha\,d\nu=y_\alpha
\qquad(\alpha\in\mathbb N^n)
\]
are equal as measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A representable full moment sequence is K-determinate when exactly one positive measure supported on K realizes all of its moments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\) is \(K\)-determinate precisely when all its \(K\)-representing measures coincide.

notation.meaning: Having a unique representing measure among measures supported on K.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Carleman and exponential-growth criteria for moment determinacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two sufficient conditions for existence and uniqueness of a representing measure for a full multivariate moment sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathbf y=(y_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n} satisfy \mathbf M_d(\mathbf y)\succeq0 for every d\ge0. If \sum_{k=1}^{\infty}[L_{\mathbf y}(x_i^{2k})]^{-1/(2k)}=+\infty for every i=1,\ldots,n, then \mathbf y has a determinate representing measure on \mathbb R^n. Alternatively, if there exist c,a>0 such that |y_\alpha|\le ca^{|\alpha|} for every \alpha\in\mathbb N^n, then \mathbf y has a determinate representing measure supported in [-a,a]^n.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive semidefinite full moment sequence is determinate when every coordinatewise Carleman series diverges. It is also determinate, with support contained in [−a,a]^n, when its moments satisfy the stated exponential-growth bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left[\forall i,\ \sum_{k=1}^{\infty}[L_{\mathbf y}(x_i^{2k})]^{-1/(2k)}=+\infty\right]\Rightarrow\mathbf y\text{ has a determinate representing measure on }\mathbb R^n;\quad\left[\exists c,a>0\ \forall\alpha,\ |y_\alpha|\le ca^{|\alpha|}\right]\Rightarrow\mathbf y\text{ has a determinate representing measure supported in }[-a,a]^n.

children.title: Moment-Indeterminate Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings admitting multiple representing measures for identical moment data.

knowledge_statements.title: Moment-Indeterminate Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniqueness of representing measures relative to a support class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and let \(y\) be a full \(K\)-representable sequence. The sequence \(y\) is \(K\)-indeterminate if there exist distinct positive Borel measures \(\mu\ne\nu\), both supported on \(K\), such that
\[
\int_Kx^\alpha\,d\mu=
\int_Kx^\alpha\,d\nu=y_\alpha
\qquad(\alpha\in\mathbb N^n).
\]
Thus indeterminacy concerns uniqueness after both the complete moment sequence and the admissible support are fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full moment sequence is K-indeterminate when two distinct positive measures supported on K realize every one of its moments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\) is \(K\)-indeterminate exactly when it has at least two distinct \(K\)-representing measures.

notation.meaning: Having multiple representing measures supported on K.

children.title: Determinacy Transition Criteria
children.top_down_role: Structural boundaries separating determinate from indeterminate moment data.

knowledge_statements.title: Determinacy Transition Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multivariate Carleman criterion ensuring moment determinacy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(y\) have a positive Borel representing measure \(\mu\) on \(\mathbb R^n\). If, for every coordinate \(i=1,\ldots,n\),
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} y_{2k e_i}^{-1/(2k)}=\infty,
\]
with a zero moment interpreted as making the corresponding term infinite, then \(\mu\) is the unique positive Borel measure on \(\mathbb R^n\) representing \(y\). Hence coordinatewise Carleman divergence places the sequence in the determinate regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A representable multisequence is determinate when the Carleman series of every coordinate's even moments diverges.
assumptions_latex: \(y\) has a positive Borel representing measure on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The representing measure of \(y\) on \(\mathbb R^n\) is unique.

notation.meaning: The ith standard basis vector of the multi-index lattice.
Even moment of the ith coordinate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sufficient Conditions for Determinacy of a Multivariate Moment Sequence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives coordinatewise Carleman and exponential-growth conditions ensuring a determinate representing measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathbf y\) be indexed by all monomials and suppose \(M_i(\mathbf y)\succeq0\) for every \(i\ge0\). If
\[
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\bigl[L_{\mathbf y}(x_i^{2k})\bigr]^{-1/(2k)}=+\infty\quad(i=1,\ldots,n),
\]
then \(\mathbf y\) has a determinate representing measure on \(\mathbb R^n\). Alternatively, if there are \(c,a>0\) such that
\[
|y_{\boldsymbol\alpha}|\le c a^{|\boldsymbol\alpha|}\quad\forall\boldsymbol\alpha\in\mathbb N^n,
\]
then \(\mathbf y\) has a determinate representing measure supported in \([-a,a]^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If all finite moment matrices are positive semidefinite, coordinatewise Carleman divergence guarantees a unique representing measure on R^n. An exponential bound by total degree also guarantees a unique representing measure supported in the corresponding box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbf y\text{ has a determinate representing measure; under the growth bound its support is contained in }[-a,a]^n

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Density Models on Compact Supports
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment characterization of densities bounded relative to a reference measure on compact support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be compact, let \(\nu\) be a finite positive Borel measure supported on \(K\) with moments \(z\), and let \(\gamma>0\). A full sequence \(y\) has a representation
\[
y_\alpha=\int_Kx^\alpha f(x)\,d\nu(x),
\qquad 0\le f\le\gamma\quad\nu\text{-almost everywhere},
\]
if and only if both \(y\) and \(\gamma z-y\) are \(K\)-moment sequences. Equivalently, their Riesz functionals are nonnegative on every polynomial nonnegative on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On compact K, moments come from a density between zero and γ relative to ν exactly when y and γz−y are both K-moment sequences.
assumptions_latex: \(\nu\) is finite, positive, supported on \(K\), and has moment sequence \(z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\) has density \(0\le f\le\gamma\) relative to \(\nu\) if and only if \(y\in\mathcal M(K)\) and \(\gamma z-y\in\mathcal M(K)\).

notation.meaning: Full moment sequence of the reference measure ν.
Radon–Nikodym density of the represented measure relative to ν.
Uniform upper bound on the density.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Density Models on Noncompact Supports
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-density characterization on noncompact supports under determinacy of the reference moments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed, possibly noncompact, and let \(\nu\) be a finite positive Borel measure supported on \(K\), possessing all moments \(z\). Assume \(z\) is \(K\)-determinate and let \(\gamma>0\). Then \(y\) has the form
\[
y_\alpha=\int_Kx^\alpha f(x)\,d\nu(x),
\qquad 0\le f\le\gamma\quad\nu\text{-almost everywhere},
\]
if and only if both \(y\) and \(\gamma z-y\) are \(K\)-moment sequences. Determinacy is essential to identify the sum of their representing measures with \(\gamma\nu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On noncompact K, the two-sequence bounded-density test is valid when the reference moment sequence is K-determinate; without determinacy, moments need not identify γν.
assumptions_latex: \(\nu\) is finite, supported on \(K\), has all moments \(z\), and \(z\) is \(K\)-determinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y=f\nu\) with \(0\le f\le\gamma\) if and only if \(y\in\mathcal M(K)\) and \(\gamma z-y\in\mathcal M(K)\).

notation.meaning: Determinate full moment sequence of the reference measure ν.
Density relative to the reference measure.
Uniform density bound.

children.title: Relaxation-Level Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Primal moment, dual certificate, and relaxation-order views at a fixed hierarchy level.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Moment SDPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense primal relaxation for polynomial minimization over a basic closed semialgebraic set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a truncated sequence \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\leq 2r}\), the order-\(r\) primal moment relaxation is
\[
\rho_r^{\mathrm{mom}}=\inf_y\left\{L_y(f):y_0=1,\ M_r(y)\succeq0,\ M_{r-d_j}(g_jy)\succeq0\ \text{for }j=1,\ldots,m\right\}.
\]
Its value is a lower bound on the polynomial infimum:
\[
\rho_r^{\mathrm{mom}}\leq\inf_{x\in K}f(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The order-r primal moment SDP minimizes the moment functional of the objective subject to normalization and positive-semidefinite moment and localizing matrices. Its value is a lower bound on the infimum over the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_r^{\mathrm{mom}}\leq\inf_{x\in K}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Riesz functional associated with the truncated sequence y
Moment matrix of order r
Localizing matrix for polynomial g_j

knowledge_statements.title: Dual SOS SDPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic dual of the dense primal moment relaxation at a fixed order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The order-\(r\) SOS dual is
\[
\rho_r^{\mathrm{sos}}=\sup_{\gamma,\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_m}\left\{\gamma:f-\gamma=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j,\ \sigma_j\in\Sigma[x],\ \deg(\sigma_0)\leq2r,\ \deg(\sigma_jg_j)\leq2r\ \text{for }j=1,\ldots,m\right\}.
\]
It is the conic dual of the corresponding order-\(r\) primal moment SDP and satisfies
\[
\rho_r^{\mathrm{sos}}\leq\rho_r^{\mathrm{mom}}\leq\inf_{x\in K}f(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The order-r SOS dual maximizes a certified lower bound subject to a degree-truncated quadratic-module representation. It is the conic dual of the primal moment SDP and satisfies weak duality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_r^{\mathrm{sos}}\leq\rho_r^{\mathrm{mom}}\leq\inf_{x\in K}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Cone of sums of squares of real polynomials
Order-r dual SOS value
Order-r primal moment value

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Order Architecture
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree truncation, nesting, and matrix growth in the dense moment-SOS hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At order \(r\), moments through degree \(2r\) are retained, the principal moment matrix has size \(s(n,r)=\binom{n+r}{r}\), and the localizing matrix for \(g_j\) has order \(r-\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil\). Increasing \(r\) enlarges the degree-truncated SOS certificate cone. Consequently, the SOS lower bounds satisfy
\[
\rho_r^{\mathrm{sos}}\leq\rho_{r+1}^{\mathrm{sos}}\leq f^*:=\inf_{x\in K}f(x)
\]
for every \(r\geq r_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order r retains moments through degree 2r and determines the sizes of the moment and localizing matrices. Increasing the order enlarges the truncated SOS certificate cone and produces nondecreasing SOS lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_r^{\mathrm{sos}}\leq\rho_{r+1}^{\mathrm{sos}}\leq f^*\) for every \(r\geq r_0\).

notation.meaning: True infimum of f over K
Order-r SOS relaxation value
Number of monomials in n variables of degree at most r
