knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix an order \(r\). If the primal moment SDP has a feasible point whose moment and required localizing matrices are positive definite relative to all imposed affine equalities, or the dual SOS SDP has an analogous strictly feasible conic representation, and both optimal values are finite, then semidefinite conic duality gives
\[
\rho_r^{\mathrm{mom}}=\rho_r^{\mathrm{sos}}.
\]
Thus there is no duality gap at that relaxation level; this statement does not by itself assert convergence as \(r\) increases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fixed order, feasibility, finite values, and Slater regularity on either side imply equality of the primal moment and dual SOS optimal values.

children.title: Levelwise Primal Attainment
children.top_down_role: Existence of optimal moment solutions at a fixed relaxation order.

knowledge_statements.title: Levelwise Primal Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-level attainment from compactness of the feasible truncated-moment set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F_r\) be the feasible set of normalized truncated moment sequences for the order-\(r\) primal SDP. If \(F_r\) is nonempty and compact, then there exists \(y^*\in F_r\) such that
\[
L_{y^*}(f)=\min_{y\in F_r}L_y(f)=\rho_r^{\mathrm{mom}}.
\]
A ball localizing constraint is a standard sufficient mechanism for boundedness when the defining semidefinite constraints make \(F_r\) closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The order-r primal moment SDP attains its minimum when its feasible set of normalized truncated moment sequences is nonempty and compact. A ball localizing constraint is a standard way to obtain boundedness.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in\mathbb{R}[x]\), and \(F_r\) is the feasible set of the order-\(r\) primal moment SDP.
\(F_r\) is nonempty, closed, and bounded in the finite-dimensional truncated-moment space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in F_r}L_y(f)\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set of truncated moment sequences at order r

children.title: Levelwise Dual Attainment

knowledge_statements.title: Levelwise Dual Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual SOS attainment supplied by primal Slater regularity at a fixed SDP order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix an order \(r\). Suppose the primal moment SDP has a feasible point lying in the relative interior of the product semidefinite cone within its affine equality space, its optimal value is finite, and the SOS dual is feasible. Then there exists a dual optimal tuple \((\gamma^*,\sigma_0^*,\ldots,\sigma_m^*)\) satisfying
\[
\gamma^*=\rho_r^{\mathrm{sos}}=\rho_r^{\mathrm{mom}}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fixed order, primal relative Slater regularity, a finite primal value, and dual feasibility ensure that an optimal finite-degree SOS certificate exists and that the primal and dual values agree.
assumptions_latex: The order-\(r\) primal moment SDP is strictly feasible relative to its affine equality constraints.
Its optimal value is finite, and the order-\(r\) dual SOS SDP is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists an optimal dual tuple \((\gamma^*,\sigma_0^*,\ldots,\sigma_m^*)\), and \(\gamma^*=\rho_r^{\mathrm{sos}}=\rho_r^{\mathrm{mom}}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an affine feasible set \(A\) and product semidefinite cone \(C\), primal Slater regularity is the predicate \(A\cap\operatorname{ri}(C)\neq\varnothing\); the dual predicate is defined analogously. Forced singular moment or localizing blocks must first be restricted to their minimal faces. If neither predicate holds, standard SDP duality no longer guarantees zero gap or attainment. Nevertheless, failure of Slater alone does not imply a gap: facial reduction may recover regularity on a proper face of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Slater regularity must be tested in the correct affine hull or minimal face. Without it, zero gap and attainment are not guaranteed, though they may still hold.

knowledge_statements.title: Putinar–Lasserre Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Putinar certificate hierarchy under the Archimedean quadratic-module hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q_r(g)\) denote the degree-\(2r\) truncation of the quadratic module \(Q(g)\), and define
\[
\rho_r=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb{R}:f-\gamma\in Q_r(g)\}.
\]
If \(Q(g)\) is Archimedean, equivalently \(R-\|x\|_2^2\in Q(g)\) for some \(R>0\), then \(K\) is compact and
\[
\rho_r\uparrow f^*:=\min_{x\in K}f(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an Archimedean quadratic module, the degree-truncated Putinar SOS bounds increase to the minimum of the polynomial over the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_r\uparrow f^*:=\min_{x\in K}f(x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Schmüdgen-Type Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preordering-based hierarchy for compact basic closed semialgebraic sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
T(g)=\left\{\sum_{\nu\in\{0,1\}^m}\sigma_\nu g_1^{\nu_1}\cdots g_m^{\nu_m}:\sigma_\nu\in\Sigma[x]\right\},
\]
and let \(T_r(g)\) contain the representations whose summands have degree at most \(2r\). Define
\[
\rho_r^{\mathrm{pre}}=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb{R}:f-\gamma\in T_r(g)\}.
\]
If \(K\) is nonempty and compact, then
\[
\rho_r^{\mathrm{pre}}\uparrow f^*:=\min_{x\in K}f(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty compact basic closed semialgebraic set, degree-truncated preorderings generated by all square-free products of the constraints give increasing lower bounds converging to the polynomial minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_r^{\mathrm{pre}}\uparrow f^*:=\min_{x\in K}f(x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Ideal-Aware Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment-SOS hierarchy retaining polynomial equalities through their generated ideal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(I_{2r}(h)=\{\sum_{k=1}^s\phi_kh_k:\deg(\phi_kh_k)\leq2r\}\), define
\[
\rho_r^I=\sup\left\{\gamma\in\mathbb{R}:f-\gamma\in Q_r(g)+I_{2r}(h)\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, the dual representation uses SOS multipliers for the inequalities and unrestricted polynomial multipliers for the equalities. The primal moment relaxation imposes
\[
L_y(x^\alpha h_k)=0\quad\text{for }|\alpha|\leq2r-\deg(h_k),\quad k=1,\ldots,s.
\]
If the quadratic module generated by \(g\) modulo \(I(h)\) is Archimedean, then
\[
\rho_r^I\uparrow f^*:=\min_{x\in K}f(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality constraints are represented by their truncated polynomial ideal, while inequalities use a truncated quadratic module. The corresponding primal relaxation imposes all compatible linear moment equations, and the bounds converge under the Archimedean hypothesis modulo the equality ideal.
assumptions_latex: The quadratic module generated by the \(g_j\), modulo the ideal \(I(h)=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_s\rangle\), is Archimedean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_r^I\uparrow f^*:=\min_{x\in K}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Ideal generated by the equality polynomials
Degree-2r truncation of the equality ideal
Degree-truncated quadratic module plus equality ideal

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The direct unconstrained SOS bound is
\[
\rho_r^{\mathrm{sos}}=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb{R}:f-\gamma\in\Sigma[x]_{2r}\}.
\]
It always satisfies \(\rho_r^{\mathrm{sos}}\leq f^*:=\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}f(x)\). However, global nonnegativity does not imply an SOS representation: for the Motzkin polynomial \(M(x,y)=x^4y^2+x^2y^4-3x^2y^2+1\), one has \(M\geq0\) and \(M\notin\Sigma[x]\). Thus direct SOS exactness, and hence general convergence, requires additional structure or weighted certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct unconstrained SOS bounds are valid but not universally exact: nonnegative polynomials such as the Motzkin polynomial need not be sums of squares.

knowledge_statements.title: Basic Semialgebraic-Set Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense Lasserre procedure for polynomial optimization over an Archimedean basic semialgebraic set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Set \(d_j=\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil\) and \(r_0=\max\{\lceil\deg(f)/2\rceil,d_1,\ldots,d_m\}\). For \(r=r_0,r_0+1,\ldots\), solve
\[
\rho_r=\inf_y\left\{L_y(f):y_0=1,\ M_r(y)\succeq0,\ M_{r-d_j}(g_jy)\succeq0\ \text{for }j=1,\ldots,m\right\}.
\]
Return the bound \(\rho_r\), together with an optimizer when attainment and its computation are established, if a prescribed certificate test or relaxation-order limit is met; otherwise increment \(r\). Under the Archimedean hypothesis, the exact bounds satisfy
\[
\rho_r\uparrow f^*:=\min_{x\in K}f(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting at the minimum admissible order, repeatedly solve the moment SDP and increase the order until a prescribed certificate test or order limit is met. Return the bound and, when available, an optimizer. Under the Archimedean hypothesis, the exact bounds converge to the minimum.
assumptions_latex: The quadratic module generated by the \(g_j\) is Archimedean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact relaxation values satisfy \(\rho_r\uparrow f^*:=\min_{x\in K}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Order-r primal moment value
Half-degree required by constraint g_j
True minimum over K

knowledge_statements.title: Homogeneous Polynomial Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sphere-normalized hierarchy for even-degree homogeneous polynomial optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\) be homogeneous of degree \(2d\), and let \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\geq0,\ j=1,\ldots,m,\ \|x\|_2^2=1\}\), where every \(g_j\) is homogeneous of even degree. For sufficiently large \(r\), define \[\rho_r=\sup\{\gamma:\ f-\gamma(\|x\|_2^2)^d\in Q_r(g)+\langle\|x\|_2^2-1\rangle_{2r}\}.\] Here \(Q_r(g)\) is the degree-\(2r\) truncated quadratic module and the subscript on the ideal denotes degree truncation. Then \(\rho_r\) is a semidefinite-computable lower bound on \(\min_{x\in K}f(x)\), and increasing \(r\) produces the homogeneous moment-SOS hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogeneity permits normalization to the unit sphere; truncated quadratic-module certificates then yield semidefinite lower bounds of increasing degree.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and the constraint polynomials are homogeneous of even degree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_r\leq\min_{x\in K}f(x)\), with a nested degree-indexed SDP hierarchy.

notation.meaning: Degree-truncated quadratic module generated by the inequalities.
Truncated ideal enforcing sphere normalization.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Set Moment Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite convergence when the feasible set itself is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{v_1,\ldots,v_s\}\subset\mathbb R^n\) be described by polynomial equalities and inequalities, and let \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\). Assume the equality ideal used by the hierarchy contains \(I(K)=\{p:p(v_i)=0\ \forall i\}\). Because interpolation supplies polynomials \(\ell_i\) satisfying \(\ell_i(v_j)=\delta_{ij}\), one has \[f-f^*=\sum_{i=1}^s\bigl(f(v_i)-f^*\bigr)\ell_i^2\pmod{I(K)},\qquad f^*=\min_i f(v_i).\] Consequently, at every relaxation order large enough to contain this identity, the moment-SOS lower bound equals \(f^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On an explicitly finite feasible set, interpolation gives a finite-degree nonnegativity certificate, so the moment hierarchy becomes exact at a finite order.
assumptions_latex: The hierarchy enforces the full vanishing ideal \(I(K)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(r_0\) such that \(\rho_r=f^*\) for every \(r\geq r_0\).

notation.meaning: Ideal of polynomials vanishing on the finite feasible set.
Lagrange interpolation polynomial for the point \(v_i\).

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports finite-set finite convergence.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-set interpolation argument is standard, but the finite-exactness theorem has no cited source or inspectable locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Dimensional Moment Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite exactness under a zero-dimensional real-radical equality ideal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\subset\mathbb R[x]\) be a zero-dimensional real-radical ideal, let \(V_{\mathbb R}(I)\) be its finite real variety, and let \(K=V_{\mathbb R}(I)\cap\{x:g_j(x)\geq0,\ j=1,ldots,m\}\neq\varnothing\). For every polynomial \(f\), the residue class of \(f-f^*\), where \(f^*=\min_{x\in K}f(x)\), admits a finite-degree weighted sum-of-squares representation modulo \(I\). Hence the moment-SOS hierarchy using the equality constraints from \(I\) and localizing constraints from \(g_j\) attains \(f^*\) at some finite relaxation order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-dimensional real-radical equality ideal reduces optimization to finitely many real points and yields finite convergence of the associated moment hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For some finite \(r_0\), every relaxation of order \(r\geq r_0\) has value \(f^*\).

notation.meaning: Real variety of the ideal.
Minimum of the objective over the feasible real variety.

review_flags: No supplied locator identifies the required zero-dimensional finite-convergence theorem.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite convergence under a radical zero-dimensional equality ideal
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite exactness of the specified SDP hierarchy for polynomial optimization over equality and inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in\mathbb R[\mathbf x]\) and \(\mathbb K=\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(\mathbf x)=0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ h_j(\mathbf x)\ge 0\ (j=1,\ldots,s)\}\). Suppose \(I=\langle g_1,\ldots,g_m\rangle\) is radical and zero-dimensional. If \(\rho_i\) denotes the optimal value of the \(i\)-th semidefinite relaxation in the hierarchy, then there exists \(i_0\in\mathbb N\) such that \(\rho_i=f_{\mathbb K}^*\) for every \(i\ge i_0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Support Algebraic Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correspondence among probability measures on a fixed finite set, simplex weights, and their moment data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix distinct points \(v_1,\ldots,v_s\in\mathbb R^n\) and set \(K=\{v_1,\ldots,v_s\}\). The map \((w_1,\ldots,w_s)\mapsto\mu=\sum_{i=1}^s w_i\delta_{v_i}\) is a bijection from \(\{w\in\mathbb R_+^s:\sum_{i=1}^s w_i=1\}\) to the probability measures supported on \(K\). The induced moments satisfy \[y_\alpha=\int_K x^\alpha\,d\mu=\sum_{i=1}^s w_i v_i^\alpha.\] Their Riesz functional annihilates \(I(K)\), and for every order \(r\), \[M_r(y)=V_r\operatorname{diag}(w)V_r^{\mathsf T},\] where the \(i\)-th column of \(V_r\) is the vector of monomials of degree at most \(r\) evaluated at \(v_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Probability measures on a fixed finite set correspond uniquely to simplex weights. Their moments are weighted point evaluations, their Riesz functionals vanish on the finite-set ideal, and their moment matrices have Vandermonde factorizations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Normalized nonnegative weights, probability measures supported on \(K\), and their induced moment sequences are in bijection.

notation.meaning: Ideal of polynomials vanishing on the finite set K.
Matrix whose columns are degree-at-most-r monomial evaluation vectors at the support points.
Dirac probability measure at the point v_i.

knowledge_statements.title: Moment LP Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral outer approximations of moment and localizing positive-semidefinite constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At order \(r\), replace each constraint \(M\succeq0\) in a moment relaxation by membership in a tractable polyhedral cone \(P_r\supseteq\mathbb S_+\). Equivalently, impose finitely many inequalities \(a_k^{\mathsf T}Ma_k\geq0\). With \(y_0=1\), the resulting problem \[\inf_y\ L_y(f)\quad\text{subject to}\quad M_r(y),\ M_{r-d_j}(g_jy)\in P_r\] is a linear program. Because every feasible moment sequence remains feasible, its value is no larger than the corresponding SDP lower bound and therefore no larger than the global minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing positive-semidefinite moment constraints by polyhedral outer approximations produces linear-programming lower bounds, generally weaker than the corresponding SDP bounds.
assumptions_latex: Each \(P_r\) is polyhedral and contains the relevant positive-semidefinite cone.
All displayed moment and localizing matrices depend affinely on \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_r^{\mathrm{LP}}\leq\rho_r^{\mathrm{SDP}}\leq f^*\).

notation.meaning: Riesz functional associated with the truncated moment vector.
Chosen polyhedral outer approximation of a PSD cone.

knowledge_statements.title: Intermediate Conic Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic bounds interpolating between LP-based and full SOS hierarchies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each order \(r\), let \(C_r^{\mathrm{LP}}\subseteq C_r\subseteq C_r^{\mathrm{SOS}}\) be nested cones of degree-bounded polynomials certified nonnegative on \(K\). Define \[\rho_r(C)=\sup\{\gamma:f-\gamma\in C_r\}.\] Then cone inclusion gives \(\rho_r(C^{\mathrm{LP}})\leq\rho_r(C)\leq\rho_r(C^{\mathrm{SOS}})\leq f^*\). If \(C_r\subseteq C_{r+1}\) after the natural degree embedding, then \(\rho_r(C)\leq\rho_{r+1}(C)\). Choosing second-order-cone or other tractable cones between the endpoints yields intermediate computational hierarchies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested nonnegativity cones yield lower bounds ordered between LP and SOS bounds; nesting across degrees makes each intermediate hierarchy monotone.
assumptions_latex: Every polynomial in \(C_r^{\mathrm{SOS}}\) is nonnegative on \(K\).
The stated cone inclusions hold at each order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_r^{\mathrm{LP}}\leq\rho_r(C)\leq\rho_r^{\mathrm{SOS}}\leq f^*\), with monotonicity under cross-order nesting.

notation.meaning: Intermediate tractable cone of certified nonnegative polynomials.
Lower bound generated by the cone C at order r.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifies the intended intermediate cone family.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Cone-inclusion monotonicity is standard, but no citation identifies or supports the intended second-order or intermediate conic hierarchy.

knowledge_statements.title: Moment-Based Upper-Bound Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Upper bounds obtained from polynomial probability densities relative to a reference measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) be compact and let \(\mu\) be a finite Borel measure with \(\operatorname{supp}\mu=K\). For \(r\geq0\), define \[u_r=\inf\left\{\int_K f(x)h(x)\,d\mu(x):h\in\Sigma[x]_{2r},\ \int_Kh\,d\mu=1\right\}.\] Every feasible \(h\) defines a probability measure \(h\,d\mu\), so \(u_r\geq f^*\). Since \(\Sigma[x]_{2r}\subseteq\Sigma[x]_{2r+2}\), one has \(u_{r+1}\leq u_r\); under full support, polynomial square densities can concentrate near a minimizer, yielding \(u_r\downarrow f^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizing expected objective values over normalized SOS polynomial densities gives decreasing upper bounds that converge to the minimum on compact full-support domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f^*\leq u_{r+1}\leq u_r\) and \(\lim_{r\to\infty}u_r=f^*\).

notation.meaning: SOS polynomials of degree at most 2r.
Order-r density-based upper bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Lower-Bound Sequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order monotonicity of nested moment-SOS lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\), and set \(f^*=\inf_{x\in K}f(x)\). Let \(Q_r(g)\) be degree-truncated certificate cones such that \(Q_r(g)\subseteq Q_{r+1}(g)\) and every element of \(Q_r(g)\) is nonnegative on \(K\). For \[\rho_r=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:f-\gamma\in Q_r(g)\},\] one has \[\rho_r\leq\rho_{r+1}\leq f^*\] at every admissible order. The analogous monotonicity holds for primal moment relaxations when every feasible order-\(r+1\) moment vector projects to a feasible order-\(r\) vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested certificate cones, or consistently nested projected moment feasible sets, produce nondecreasing lower bounds on the global infimum.
assumptions_latex: Every element of \(Q_r(g)\) is nonnegative on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_r\leq\rho_{r+1}\leq f^*\) for every admissible order \(r\).

knowledge_statements.title: Moment-Solution Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subsequential convergence of optimal truncated moments to optimal representing measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\geq0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), let \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\), and assume the associated quadratic module is Archimedean. For every sufficiently large order \(r\), let \(y^{(r)}\) be an optimal normalized moment vector with \(y^{(r)}_0=1\), and assume the relaxation values converge to \(f^*=\min_{x\in K}f(x)\). The fixed-coordinate families \(\{y^{(r)}_\alpha:r\geq |\alpha|/2\}\) are bounded. Every diagonal accumulation sequence \(y^*=(y^*_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n}\) is the moment sequence of a probability measure \(\mu^*\) on \(K\) satisfying \[\int_K f\,d\mu^*=f^*.\] Thus \(\mu^*\) is supported on the global minimizer set. If the minimizer is unique, say \(x^*\), then for every fixed \(\alpha\in\mathbb N^n\), \[\lim_{r\to\infty}y^{(r)}_\alpha=(x^*)^\alpha.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-coordinate accumulation points of optimal relaxation moments represent probability measures supported on global minimizers. A unique minimizer forces coordinatewise convergence to its moment sequence.
assumptions_latex: The quadratic module generated by the constraints is Archimedean.
An optimal normalized moment vector exists at every sufficiently large order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every diagonal moment-limit measure is optimal; if the minimizer \(x^*\) is unique, then \(y^{(r)}_\alpha\to(x^*)^\alpha\) for every fixed \(\alpha\).

knowledge_statements.title: Archimedean Quadratic-Module Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic boundedness condition supporting Putinar-type convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)\subset\mathbb R[x]\), define \[Q(g)=\left\{\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j:\sigma_j\in\Sigma[x]\right\}.\] The quadratic module is Archimedean when there exists \(R>0\) such that \[R-\|x\|_2^2\in Q(g).\] This condition implies that \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\geq0\ \forall j\}\) lies in the closed ball of radius \(\sqrt R\), hence is compact. In this regime every polynomial strictly positive on \(K\) belongs to \(Q(g)\), which supplies the positivity certificates used for asymptotic moment-SOS convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic module is Archimedean when it certifies a ball constraint; this makes the feasible set compact and enables strict-positivity certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R-\|x\|_2^2\in Q(g)\) for some \(R>0\), implying compactness of \(K\) and Putinar positivity certificates.

notation.meaning: Quadratic module generated by the constraint polynomials.

knowledge_statements.title: Noncompact Convergence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the unconstrained SOS hierarchy on a noncompact domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\mathbb R^2\) and \(M(x,y)=x^4y^2+x^2y^4-3x^2y^2+1\). Then \(M\ge 0\) on \(K\), \(\min_K M=0\), and \(M\) is not a sum of squares. For \(d\ge 3\), define \(\rho_d=\sup\{\gamma\in\mathbb R:M-\gamma\in\Sigma[x,y]_{2d}\}\), with \(\sup\varnothing=-\infty\). The sequence \((\rho_d)\) cannot converge to \(0\): otherwise closedness of the finite-degree SOS cone, together with the impossibility of canceling higher-degree leading terms among squares, would imply \(M\in\Sigma[x,y]\). Thus noncompactness without an additional positivity certificate permits a persistent relaxation gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonnegative Motzkin polynomial is not SOS, so the unconstrained SOS hierarchy on the noncompact plane need not converge to its true minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_d\not\to\min_K M=0\).

notation.meaning: Sums of polynomial squares having degree at most 2d.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Qualification Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LICQ at every global minimizer of a polynomial optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:h_i(x)=0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ g_j(x)\ge 0\ (j=1,\ldots,s)\}\). The constraint-qualification regime holds at a global minimizer \(u\in K\) when the vectors \(\{\nabla h_i(u):1\le i\le m\}\cup\{\nabla g_j(u):g_j(u)=0\}\) are linearly independent. It holds for the optimization problem when this condition is satisfied at every global minimizer. Under this condition, each global minimizer admits uniquely determined KKT multipliers whenever the first-order KKT stationarity equation is solvable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each global minimizer, equality gradients and gradients of active inequalities must be linearly independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{\nabla h_i(u)\}_i\cup\{\nabla g_j(u):g_j(u)=0\}\text{ is linearly independent}.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Complementarity Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict complementarity for active polynomial inequalities at every global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:h_i(x)=0\ (i=1,\ldots,m),\ g_j(x)\ge 0\ (j=1,\ldots,s)\}\). At a global minimizer \(u\in K\), strict complementarity holds if there exist KKT multipliers \((\lambda,\mu)\) satisfying \(
abla f(u)=\sum_i\lambda_i
abla h_i(u)+\sum_j\mu_j
abla g_j(u)\), \(\mu_j\ge0\), and \(\mu_jg_j(u)=0\), such that \(g_j(u)=0\) implies \(\mu_j>0\). The strict-complementarity regime holds when every global minimizer admits such multipliers. If LICQ holds at \(u\), these KKT multipliers are unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every global minimizer, there must be KKT multipliers for which each active inequality has a strictly positive multiplier; under LICQ, the multipliers are unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists(\lambda,\mu)\text{ satisfying the KKT conditions such that }g_j(u)=0\Longrightarrow\mu_j>0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order-Sufficiency Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive Lagrangian curvature on the active-constraint tangent space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(u\) satisfy the KKT conditions for \(K=\{x:h_i(x)=0,\ g_j(x)\ge0\}\), and define \(L(x)=f(x)-\sum_i\lambda_i h_i(x)-\sum_j\mu_j g_j(x)\). The second-order sufficiency condition holds at \(u\) when \(v^T
abla_{xx}^2L(u)v>0\) for every nonzero \(v\) satisfying \(
abla h_i(u)^Tv=0\) for all \(i\) and \(
abla g_j(u)^Tv=0\) for every active \(j\). The regime requires this condition at every global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lagrangian Hessian must be positive definite along every nonzero tangent direction at each global minimizer.
assumptions_latex: KKT conditions hold at every global minimizer.
Active-constraint gradients define the stated tangent space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v\ne0\text{ and }v\in T_u\Longrightarrow v^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(u)v>0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary-Hessian Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite convergence from Marshall's boundary-Hessian condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x:h(x)=0,\ g(x)\ge0\}\), assume \(I(h)+Q(g)\) is archimedean, and let \(f^*=\min_K f\). Suppose the boundary-Hessian condition holds at every global minimizer: in suitable local parameters, the linear coefficients along active inequality parameters are positive and the quadratic part along the remaining local parameters is positive definite. Then \(f-f^*\in I(h)+Q(g)\). Consequently, some truncation order \(r\) satisfies \(f-f^*\in I_{2r}(h)+Q_r(g)\), and the order-\(r\) moment/SOS relaxation has value \(f^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An archimedean problem satisfying the boundary-Hessian condition at all minimizers has an exact finite-order moment/SOS relaxation.
assumptions_latex: The boundary-Hessian condition holds at every point in \(\operatorname*{argmin}_K f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists r:\ f-f^*\in I_{2r}(h)+Q_r(g)\), hence \(\rho_r=f^*\).

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Variety Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite convergence when the equality variety is finite and real radical.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=I(h)\subset\mathbb R[x]\) be real radical with finite real variety \(V_{\mathbb R}(I)\), let \(K=V_{\mathbb R}(I)\cap\{x:g_j(x)\ge0\}\), and suppose \(K\ne\varnothing\). For every polynomial \(f\), writing \(f^*=\min_K f\), there exists a finite degree \(2r\) for which \(f-f^*\in I_{2r}(h)+Q_r(g)\). Therefore the order-\(r\) moment/SOS relaxation is exact; moreover, an optimal moment sequence can be represented by a probability measure supported on the finitely many global minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A real-radical finite equality variety forces exactness at some finite relaxation order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists r:\rho_r=f^*=\min_{x\in K}f(x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Set Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness for a hierarchy using the vanishing ideal of a finite feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{u_1,\ldots,u_N\}\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and let \(I(K)=\{p:p(u)=0\text{ for all }u\in K\}\). For every \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\), set \(f^*=\min_{u\in K}f(u)\). There exist interpolation polynomials \(\ell_i\) with \(\ell_i(u_j)=\delta_{ij}\), so \(f-f^*\equiv\sum_{i=1}^N(f(u_i)-f^*)\ell_i^2\pmod{I(K)}\). Hence \(f-f^*\in I(K)+\Sigma[x]\), and a sufficiently high truncation of the associated moment/SOS hierarchy is exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite feasible set, interpolation expresses the objective gap as SOS modulo the set's vanishing ideal, giving finite exactness.
assumptions_latex: The hierarchy includes the vanishing ideal \(I(K)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists r:\ f-f^*\in I(K)_{2r}+\Sigma[x]_{2r}\), hence \(\rho_r=f^*\).

notation.meaning: Vanishing ideal of the finite set K.

knowledge_statements.title: Variety–Set Exactness Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-algebra equivalence underlying finite-variety and finite-set exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\subset\mathbb R[x]\) be real radical and suppose \(K=V_{\mathbb R}(I)=\{u_1,\ldots,u_N\}\). Evaluation induces an algebra isomorphism \(\mathbb R[x]/I\cong\mathbb R^N\), given by \([p]\mapsto(p(u_1),\ldots,p(u_N))\). Under this isomorphism, a residue class is nonnegative on \(K\) exactly when it is a sum of squares in \(\mathbb R[x]/I\). Equivalently, \(p\ge0\) on \(K\) if and only if \(p\in I+\Sigma[x]\). Thus finite-variety exactness and finite-set interpolation exactness are the same certificate in two representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite real-radical variety, evaluation identifies its coordinate algebra with functions on the finite set, and nonnegativity with SOS modulo the ideal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\ge0\text{ on }K\Longleftrightarrow p\in I+\Sigma[x]\).

notation.meaning: Real coordinate algebra of the variety.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix the numbers and degree bounds of the polynomial objective and constraints, and restrict to coefficient tuples for which \(I(h)+Q(g)\) is archimedean and the feasible set is nonempty. For every such generic tuple, there exists \(r<\infty\) such that \(f-f^*\in I_{2r}(h)+Q_r(g)\). Consequently, Lasserre's hierarchy attains the global minimum at a finite relaxation order.

knowledge_statements.title: Positivity-Certificate Degree Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degree bounds for strictly positive polynomials on an archimedean basic closed set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\ge0\}\subset[-1,1]^n\), assume \(Q(g)\) is archimedean, and let \(p\) have degree at most \(m\), coefficient norm at most \(H\), and minimum \(p_{\min}\ge\delta>0\) on \(K\). A quantitative archimedean Positivstellensatz supplies a finite bound \(D=D(n,m,H/\delta,g)\) such that \(p\in Q(g)\) has a representation whose products \(\sigma_jg_j\) have degree at most \(D\). Hence relaxation order \(r\ge\lceil D/2\rceil\) certifies \(p
onnegative 0\) on \(K\). Dependence on the positivity margin cannot generally be omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict positivity, coefficient size, dimension, degrees, and constraint geometry determine a finite certificate-degree bound and thus a sufficient hierarchy order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\in Q_{\lceil D/2\rceil}(g)\) for some \(D=D(n,m,H/\delta,g)<\infty\).

notation.meaning: Quadratic module truncated at degree 2r.
Strict positivity margin of p on K.
Upper bound on certificate degree.

knowledge_statements.title: Hierarchy Convergence-Rate Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of positivity-certificate bounds into relaxation-error rates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f^*=\min_K f\), let \(\rho_r\) be the order-\(r\) SOS lower bound, and define \(D(\varepsilon)\) as any degree bound guaranteeing \(f-f^*+\varepsilon\in Q(g)\) with certificate degree at most \(D(\varepsilon)\). Then \(2r\ge D(\varepsilon)\) implies \(0\le f^*-\rho_r\le\varepsilon\). Consequently, polynomial certificate growth \(D(\varepsilon)\le C\varepsilon^{-a}\) yields \(f^*-\rho_r\le(C/(2r))^{1/a}\), while logarithmic growth \(D(\varepsilon)\le C\log(B/\varepsilon)\) yields \(f^*-\rho_r\le B e^{-2r/C}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverting a degree bound for the perturbed objective produces algebraic, exponential, or other convergence-rate families for hierarchy values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(2r\ge D(\varepsilon)\Longrightarrow 0\le f^*-\rho_r\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Certificate-degree bound at tolerance epsilon.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Exactness Order Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate degree gives an explicit sufficient order for finite exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the polynomial problem with optimum \(f^*\) and truncated certificates \(I_{2r}(h)+Q_r(g)\). If a finite certificate \(f-f^*=\sum_i\phi_i h_i+\sigma_0+\sum_j\sigma_jg_j\) satisfies \(\deg(\phi_i h_i)\le2R\), \(\deg(\sigma_0)\le2R\), and \(\deg(\sigma_jg_j)\le2R\), where every \(\sigma_j\) is SOS, then every relaxation order \(r\ge R\) is exact: \(\rho_r=f^*\). Thus one valid exactness-order bound is half the maximum degree among the terms of any known optimality certificate, rounded upward.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A degree-2R certificate for the objective gap guarantees exactness at order R and at every higher order.
assumptions_latex: The displayed ideal-plus-quadratic-module certificate exists with maximum degree at most \(2R\).

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Convergence Decision Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes bounded-order exactness testing from the unbounded existential finite-convergence problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a polynomial optimization instance encoded by rational data, let \(\rho_k\) be the order-\(k\) moment-relaxation value and \(f^*\) its global optimum. The bounded problem asks whether \(\rho_k=f^*\) for a supplied \(k\); the finite-convergence problem asks whether \(\exists k\in\mathbb N:\rho_k=f^*\). These are different decision problems: an algorithm for the bounded problem at any fixed order does not decide the unbounded existential problem unless it is accompanied by a computable instance-dependent upper bound on an exact order. Consequently, no complexity classification is meaningful without fixing the encoding, feasibility assumptions, equality test, and whether the relaxation order is bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Testing exactness at a given order differs from deciding whether some exact order exists; the latter requires an effective order bound for bounded searches to decide it.
assumptions_latex: The input polynomials have rational coefficients and a specified finite encoding.
The hierarchy values and the global optimum are interpreted as exact real numbers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bounded-order exactness complexity alone does not classify the decision problem \(\exists k\in\mathbb N:\rho_k=f^*\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive and Flat Extensions of a Moment Matrix
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines one-order positive extensions of truncated moment sequences and the rank-preserving flatness condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathbf y=(y_{\boldsymbol\alpha})_{|\boldsymbol\alpha|\le2r}\) satisfy \(M_r(\mathbf y)\succeq0\). A positive extension chooses moments \(y_{\boldsymbol\beta}\) for \(2r<|\boldsymbol\beta|\le2(r+1)\) so that the extended sequence satisfies \(M_{r+1}(\mathbf y)\succeq0\). It is a flat extension if, additionally,
\[
\operatorname{rank}M_{r+1}(\mathbf y)=\operatorname{rank}M_r(\mathbf y).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive extension augments a truncated sequence through the next two degrees while preserving positive semidefiniteness of the enlarged moment matrix. It is flat when the enlarged matrix has the same rank as the original matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_{r+1}(\mathbf y)\succeq0\text{ defines a positive extension, and }\operatorname{rank}M_{r+1}(\mathbf y)=\operatorname{rank}M_r(\mathbf y)\text{ defines a flat extension}

knowledge_statements.title: Curto–Fialkow Flat Extension Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real multivariate truncated moment theorem for a positive semidefinite flat moment matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le 2d}\) be a real truncated multisequence with \(y_0=1\). If \(M_d(y)\succeq0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}M_d(y)=\operatorname{rank}M_{d-1}(y)=r\), then \(y\) has a unique representing measure of the form \(\mu=\sum_{i=1}^{r}w_i\delta_{x^{(i)}}\), where the points \(x^{(i)}\in\mathbb R^n\) are distinct and \(w_i>0\). Thus \(y_\alpha=\int x^\alpha\,d\mu\) for every \(|\alpha|\le2d\), and the moment sequence extends to all degrees with moment matrices of rank \(r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive semidefinite moment matrix whose rank stops growing has a unique representing measure with exactly that many atoms and a rank-preserving full extension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is a unique \(r\)-atomic representing measure on \(\mathbb R^n\), and \(y\) admits a rank-\(r\) full moment extension.

notation.meaning: moment matrix indexed by monomials of degree at most d
Dirac measure at x
stable moment-matrix rank

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Flat Extension Theorem for Truncated Moment Sequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes finite atomic representing measures on real multivariate space through positive semidefinite flat extensions of truncated moment matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbf y=(y_{\boldsymbol\alpha})_{|\boldsymbol\alpha|\le 2r}\) be a truncated multisequence. Then \(\mathbf y\) admits a \(\operatorname{rank}M_r(\mathbf y)\)-atomic representing measure \(\mu\) on \(\mathbb R^n\) if and only if \(M_r(\mathbf y)\succeq 0\) and \(M_r(\mathbf y)\) admits a positive semidefinite flat extension \(M_{r+1}(\widetilde{\mathbf y})\succeq 0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A truncated multisequence has a representing measure on real n-space supported on as many atoms as the rank of its order-r moment matrix if and only if that moment matrix is positive semidefinite and admits a positive semidefinite flat extension of order r+1.
assumptions_latex: \(M_r(\mathbf y)\) is its order-\(r\) moment matrix
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbf y\text{ admits a }\operatorname{rank}M_r(\mathbf y)\text{-atomic representing measure on }\mathbb R^n\iff M_r(\mathbf y)\succeq0\text{ and }M_r(\mathbf y)\text{ admits a flat extension }M_{r+1}(\widetilde{\mathbf y})\succeq0.\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes truncated moment sequences having an atomic representing measure whose number of atoms equals the moment-matrix rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathbf y=(y_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb N_{2d}^n} and let r=\operatorname{rank}\mathbf M_d(\mathbf y). knowledge_statements.title: Recursively Generated Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kernel-propagation condition for truncated moment matrices and their rank-preserving extensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A truncated moment matrix \(M_d(y)\) is recursively generated if, whenever a polynomial \(p\) of degree at most \(d\) has coefficient vector in \(\ker M_d(y)\), every polynomial \(pq\) with \(\deg(pq)\le d\) also has coefficient vector in \(\ker M_d(y)\). An extension \(M_{d+1}(\widetilde y)\) is a recursively generated flat extension when it extends \(M_d(y)\), satisfies \(M_{d+1}(\widetilde y)\succeq0\), preserves rank, and obeys this kernel-propagation rule through degree \(d+1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Kernel polynomial relations must remain valid after multiplication whenever the product stays within the truncation; a flat extension preserves both these relations and rank.
assumptions_latex: \(M_d(y)\) is indexed by all monomials of degree at most \(d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The kernel relations form a truncated ideal, and a recursively generated flat extension propagates them without increasing rank.

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Constrained Flat Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Flat-extension criterion producing a finitely atomic measure supported on a basic closed semialgebraic set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), set \(d_K=\max\{1,\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil:j=1,\ldots,m\}\), and let \(y\) be truncated through degree \(2k\). If \(M_k(y)\succeq0\), every localizing matrix \(M_{k-\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil}(g_jy)\succeq0\), and \(\operatorname{rank}M_k(y)=\operatorname{rank}M_{k-d_K}(y)=r\), then \(y\) has an \(r\)-atomic representing measure supported on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive moment and localizing matrices plus rank stability yield a finitely atomic representing measure whose atoms satisfy every defining inequality of the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: The stated moment and localizing matrices are positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist \(x^{(i)}\in K\) and \(w_i>0\) such that \(y_\alpha=\sum_{i=1}^r w_i(x^{(i)})^\alpha\) for all \(|\alpha|\le2k\).

children.title: Sparse Flat Extensions
children.top_down_role: Flat-extension regimes retaining selected sparse moment structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Flat Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clique-wise flatness criterion for sparse moment data under consistent overlaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let variable cliques \(I_1,\ldots,I_s\) satisfy the running-intersection property, and let each clique carry a truncated moment sequence \(y^{(\ell)}\) through degree \(2k\). A sparse flat extension condition consists of \(M_k(y^{(\ell)})\succeq0\), \(\operatorname{rank}M_k(y^{(\ell)})=\operatorname{rank}M_{k-1}(y^{(\ell)})\) for every \(\ell\), and equality of the induced truncated moments on every overlap \(I_\ell\cap I_q\). Each clique then admits a finite atomic marginal measure; a global atomic measure follows only when those marginal measures can be coupled consistently on the clique tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each clique moment matrix must be flat, and overlap moments and atomic marginals must agree; clique-wise flatness alone does not guarantee a global representing measure.
assumptions_latex: The clique family satisfies the running-intersection property.
All clique sequences use a common truncation order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Clique-wise atomic measures exist; global sparse extraction additionally requires a consistent coupling of their overlap marginals.

notation.meaning: variable-index set of clique ell
truncated clique moment sequence

knowledge_statements.title: Border-Basis Flat Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-preserving extension expressed through a monomial basis and its border relations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be a finite monomial set containing \(1\) and connected to \(1\), with border \(\partial B=(x_1B\cup\cdots\cup x_nB)\setminus B\). A border-basis flat extension is specified by a nonsingular moment block \(H_B=(y_{\beta+\gamma})_{\beta,\gamma\in B}\) and reduction relations \(b-\sum_{c\in B}a_{bc}c\in\ker H\) for every \(b\in\partial B\), such that the induced multiplication matrices on \(\operatorname{span}B\) commute and are self-adjoint for the bilinear form defined by \(H_B\). If \(H_B\succ0\), their joint real spectrum yields a positive atomic representing measure with \(|B|\) atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Border monomials reduce to a basis, and commuting self-adjoint multiplication matrices produce a positive atomic measure without increasing the moment rank.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is finite, contains \(1\), and is connected to \(1\).
The moment block \(H_B\) is positive definite.
Border reductions are available for every element of \(\partial B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Commuting self-adjoint reductions define a rank-\(|B|\) flat extension and a positive measure supported on their joint spectrum.

notation.meaning: chosen monomial basis
monomial border of B
moment block indexed by B

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The border-basis formulation is plausible and fits a condition container, but no source supports the precise equivalence among border reductions, commuting self-adjoint multiplication matrices, a flat extension, and exactly |B| atoms. The domain of the partially specified moment functional also needs authoritative formulation.

children.title: Sparse–Border Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility between sparse moment patterns and border-basis closures.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse–Border Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility predicate for gluing clique-wise border-basis moment extensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each clique \(I_\ell\), let \(B_\ell\) be a connected monomial basis with border reductions and multiplication operators \(X_i^{(\ell)}\) for \(i\in I_\ell\). Sparse and border structures are compatible when, for every overlap \(I_\ell\cap I_q\), the restricted moment functionals agree and the operators representing every shared variable agree after identifying the common quotient space. Equivalently, shared border relations reduce to the same residue classes on both cliques. Under running intersection and consistent positive atomic overlap marginals, the clique representations can be glued; without operator-level agreement, separate flat extensions need not define one global quotient representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overlapping cliques must agree on both moments and reductions of shared variables; otherwise their individually flat border representations may fail to glue globally.
assumptions_latex: The clique family satisfies running intersection.
Each clique has a positive border-basis flat extension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global gluing is permitted only when shared moment functionals and shared-variable multiplication operators coincide on every overlap.

notation.meaning: monomial basis for clique ell
clique multiplication operator for variable i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed operator-level compatibility predicate is specialized, and the claimed gluing implication depends on precise identifications of overlap quotient spaces and marginal consistency. No citation supports those hypotheses or the conclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Flat-Truncation Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori certificate for exactness and optimizer extraction from an optimal moment relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f\) on \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), and let \(y^*\) solve the order-\(k\) moment relaxation with \(y^*_0=1\). Put \(d_f=\lceil\deg(f)/2\rceil\) and \(d_K=\max\{1,\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil:j=1,\ldots,m\}\). If some \(t\), with \(\max\{d_f,d_K\}\le t\le k\), satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}M_t(y^*)=\operatorname{rank}M_{t-d_K}(y^*)=r\), then the feasible moment and localizing matrices certify an \(r\)-atomic measure supported on \(K\). Its atoms are global minimizers, its integral of \(f\) equals the relaxation value, and that value equals the true minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank stability at a truncation containing the objective degree, together with moment and localizing feasibility, certifies exactness and permits extraction of finitely many global minimizers.
assumptions_latex: The order-\(k\) moment relaxation has an optimal solution \(y^*\) with \(y^*_0=1\).
All required moment and localizing matrices of \(y^*\) are positive semidefinite.
There is an order \(t\) satisfying \(\max\{d_f,d_K\}\le t\le k\) and the displayed flat-truncation rank equality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxation is exact and the \(r\) support points extracted from \(y^*\) are global minimizers.

half-degree order needed to evaluate the objective

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Convergence Consequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consequences of detecting flat truncation at a finite relaxation order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d_f=\lceil\deg(f)/2\rceil\). If an optimal order-\(k\) moment solution \(y^*\) satisfies a support-constrained flat-truncation condition at some \(t\) with \(d_f\le t\le k\), then the hierarchy has finite convergence at order \(k\): \(\rho_k=f^*\). Moreover, the stable rank equals the number of atoms in a representing measure for the truncation, every atom is feasible, and every atom with positive weight is a global minimizer because their weighted average objective equals \(f^*\) while each feasible objective value is at least \(f^*\). Multiplication matrices constructed from a column basis recover the atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A flat optimal truncation that contains the objective degree proves finite convergence, counts the extracted atoms, and identifies their support points as global minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(y^*\) is optimal and feasible for the order-\(k\) moment relaxation.
A support-constrained flat-truncation equality holds at some \(t\) satisfying \(d_f\le t\le k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_k=f^*\), and the stable-rank many atoms extracted from \(y^*\) are feasible global minimizers.

notation.meaning: half-degree order needed to evaluate the objective
order-k relaxation value
true global minimum

knowledge_statements.title: Converse Implication Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite convergence does not force flatness of every optimal moment solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{0:x\in[-1,1]\}\). Every order of the moment hierarchy is exact because both the true optimum and every relaxation value equal \(0\). For each order \(k\), truncate the moments of normalized Lebesgue measure on \([-1,1]\) to obtain an optimal feasible sequence \(y^{(k)}\). Its moment matrix satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}M_t(y^{(k)})=t+1\) for every \(t\le k\), since no nonzero polynomial of degree at most \(t\) vanishes almost everywhere on the interval. Hence \(\operatorname{rank}M_t(y^{(k)})\ne\operatorname{rank}M_{t-1}(y^{(k)})\), so these optimal solutions have no flat truncation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant objective on an interval has finite convergence, yet optimal moments from Lebesgue measure have increasing ranks and are never flat.
assumptions_latex: The standard moment hierarchy for the constraint \(1-x^2\ge0\) is used.
Moments are taken from normalized Lebesgue measure on \([-1,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite convergence of relaxation values does not imply flat truncation of every optimal moment solution.

notation.meaning: degree-2k truncation of normalized Lebesgue moments
univariate moment matrix through order t

knowledge_statements.title: Flat Truncation in Asymptotic Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates asymptotic value convergence from finite rank stabilization of moment solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a moment hierarchy has values \(\rho_k\uparrow f^*\) and optimal truncated sequences \(y^{(k)}\). Asymptotic convergence of the values alone implies neither that some finite \(y^{(k)}\) has a flat truncation nor that every coordinatewise limit moment sequence is finitely atomic. More precisely, if a subsequence has moments converging in every fixed degree to a full moment sequence \(\bar y\) represented by a measure with infinite support, then the ranks \(\operatorname{rank}M_t(\bar y)\) are unbounded as \(t\to\infty\), so \(\bar y\) has no eventually flat moment matrices. Flat truncation in an asymptotic regime therefore requires additional rank, algebraic, or finite-support structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convergence of hierarchy values does not itself produce finite-rank moments; a coordinatewise limiting measure with infinite support cannot have eventually flat moment matrices.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation values converge monotonically to the true optimum.
Optimal truncated sequences exist at the considered orders.
Whenever a limit sequence is discussed, a subsequence converges coordinatewise in every fixed degree to a full represented moment sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The implication \(\rho_k\to f^*\Rightarrow\) eventual flat truncation is invalid without additional rank or support assumptions.

notation.meaning: order-k relaxation value
an optimal truncated moment sequence at order k
a full moment sequence obtained as a coordinatewise subsequential limit

knowledge_statements.title: Putinar Flat-Truncation Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Flat-truncation certificate for moment relaxations based on an Archimedean quadratic module.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) and assume the quadratic module \(Q(g)\) is Archimedean. In the order-\(k\) Putinar moment relaxation, let \(y^*\) be optimal with \(y^*_0=1\), \(M_k(y^*)\succeq0\), and \(M_{k-d_j}(g_jy^*)\succeq0\), where \(d_j=\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil\). Define \(d_f=\lceil\deg(f)/2\rceil\) and \(d_K=\max\{1,d_1,\ldots,d_m\}\). If, for some \(t\) with \(\max\{d_f,d_K\}\le t\le k\), \(\operatorname{rank}M_t(y^*)=\operatorname{rank}M_{t-d_K}(y^*)\), then \(y^*\) yields a finite atomic measure on \(K\); the relaxation is exact and its atoms are global minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within an Archimedean Putinar hierarchy, normalized feasible moments, localizing positivity, and a shifted rank equality at an order containing the objective certify exactness and finite extraction of global minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(y^*\) is normalized, optimal, and feasible for the order-\(k\) Putinar relaxation.
There is an order \(t\) satisfying \(\max\{d_f,d_K\}\le t\le k\) and the stated shifted flat-truncation equality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The order-\(k\) Putinar relaxation is exact and admits extraction of a finite atomic optimal measure supported on \(K\).

knowledge_statements.title: Jacobian Flat-Truncation Families

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Atomic Measure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines an s-atomic measure independently of any recovery procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A measure \(\mu\) is \(s\)-atomic if there are pairwise distinct points \(z_1,\ldots,z_s\) and weights \(w_1,\ldots,w_s>0\) such that
\[
\mu=\sum_{j=1}^{s}w_j\delta_{z_j}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An s-atomic measure is a positive linear combination of Dirac measures at s distinct atoms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mu=\sum_{j=1}^{s}w_j\delta_{z_j}\text{ is an }s\text{-atomic measure}

knowledge_statements.title: Moment-Matrix Rank
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank of a truncated multivariate moment matrix indexed by bounded-degree monomials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a real truncated sequence \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le2t}\), the order-\(t\) moment matrix is \(M_t(y)=(y_{\alpha+\beta})_{|\alpha|,|\beta|\le t}\). Its moment-matrix rank is \(r_t(y)=\operatorname{rank}M_t(y)\), equivalently the dimension of the column space generated by monomials of degree at most \(t\), or the codimension of \(\ker M_t(y)\) in \(\mathbb R[x]_{\le t}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Moment-matrix rank is the dimension of the independent moment columns indexed by monomials through the truncation order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_t(y)=\dim\operatorname{col}M_t(y)=\dim\mathbb R[x]_{\le t}-\dim\ker M_t(y)\).

notation.meaning: Order-t moment matrix.
Rank of the order-t moment matrix.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Flat-extension criterion for a supported atomic representing measure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes truncated moment sequences admitting a finite atomic representing measure on a basic semialgebraic set and counts atoms on each constraint boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge 0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}, where \deg g_j\in\{2v_j-1,2v_j\}, and let v=\max_j v_j with d\ge v. For y=(y_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb N_{2d}^n}, there exists a representing measure \mu supported on K with exactly \operatorname{rank}M_{d-v}(y) atoms if and only if M_d(y)\succeq0, M_{d-v}(g_jy)\succeq0 for every j, and \operatorname{rank}M_d(y)=\operatorname{rank}M_{d-v}(y). Moreover, for each j, exactly \operatorname{rank}M_d(y)-\operatorname{rank}M_{d-v}(g_jy) atoms of \mu satisfy g_j(x)=0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A truncated moment sequence has an atomic representing measure supported on K, with cardinality equal to the lower-order moment-matrix rank, exactly when the stated moment and localizing matrices are positive semidefinite and the moment matrix is flat. For each constraint, the stated rank difference counts the atoms on its boundary.
assumptions_latex: y=(y_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb N_{2d}^n},\quad v=\max_{1\le j\le m}v_j,\quad d\ge v
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\mu:\ \operatorname{supp}\mu\subseteq K,\ |\operatorname{supp}\mu|=\operatorname{rank}M_{d-v}(y)\iff\left[M_d(y)\succeq0,\ M_{d-v}(g_jy)\succeq0\ \forall j,\ \operatorname{rank}M_d(y)=\operatorname{rank}M_{d-v}(y)\right],\quad |\{x\in\operatorname{supp}\mu:g_j(x)=0\}|=\operatorname{rank}M_d(y)-\operatorname{rank}M_{d-v}(g_jy)\ \forall j.

knowledge_statements.title: Atomic Support Cardinality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Number of distinct positive-mass points in a finite atomic representing measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite positive atomic measure on \(\mathbb R^n\) has the form \(\mu=\sum_{i=1}^{r}w_i\delta_{x^{(i)}}\), where \(w_i>0\) and the points \(x^{(i)}\) are pairwise distinct. Its atomic support is \(\operatorname{supp}\mu=\{x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(r)}\}\), and its atomic support cardinality is \(|\operatorname{supp}\mu|=r\). Repeated locations are first combined and zero-weight terms discarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Atomic support cardinality counts the distinct locations carrying strictly positive mass after redundant terms are removed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\operatorname{supp}\mu|=r\).

knowledge_statements.title: Rank–Cardinality Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality between stable moment rank and the number of atoms in a flat representing measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le2t}\) satisfy \(M_t(y)\succeq0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}M_t(y)=\operatorname{rank}M_{t-1}(y)=r\). Then \(y\) has a unique positive representing measure \(\mu=\sum_{i=1}^{r}w_i\delta_{x^{(i)}}\) through degree \(2t\), with distinct atoms and positive weights. Consequently, \(|\operatorname{supp}\mu|=r=\operatorname{rank}M_t(y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under positive semidefiniteness and flatness, the stable moment rank equals the exact number of atoms in the representing measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\) has a unique \(r\)-atomic representing measure and \(|\operatorname{supp}\mu|=\operatorname{rank}M_t(y)=r\).

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Rank Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Situations where a displayed atomic sum does not have cardinality equal to truncated moment rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mu=\sum_{i=1}^{s}w_i\delta_{x^{(i)}}\), the moment matrix factors as \(M_t(y)=V_t\operatorname{diag}(w)V_t^{\mathsf T}\), where \(V_t\) evaluates degree-at-most-\(t\) monomials at the listed points. Hence \(\operatorname{rank}M_t(y)\le |\operatorname{supp}\mu|\le s\). Equality can fail if locations repeat, weights vanish, or \(V_t\) lacks full column rank. For example, at \(t=0\), every nonzero positive measure has \(\operatorname{rank}M_0(y)=1\), regardless of how many support points it has.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank can underestimate listed or actual atoms when terms are redundant or the truncation cannot distinguish the support points.
assumptions_latex: \(y\) consists of the moments of a finite nonnegative atomic measure through degree \(2t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}M_t(y)\le |\operatorname{supp}\mu|\), with equality requiring positive distinct atoms and full column rank of \(V_t\).

knowledge_statements.title: Atomic Support Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of atomic support as the real zero set of the flat moment-kernel ideal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(M_t(y)\succeq0\) is flat with rank \(r\), and let \(\mu=\sum_{i=1}^{r}w_i\delta_{x^{(i)}}\) be its representing measure. Extend the truncated kernel relations by multiplication and reduction to the zero-dimensional ideal \(I_y\). Then \(I_y=I(\operatorname{supp}\mu)\), and the atomic support has the geometric representation \[\operatorname{supp}\mu=V_{\mathbb R}(I_y)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:p(x)=0\text{ for every }p\in I_y\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a flat moment sequence, the atoms are precisely the common real zeros of the ideal generated by moment-kernel relations.
assumptions_latex: \(I_y\) denotes the ideal closure of the flat kernel relations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I_y=I(\operatorname{supp}\mu)\) and \(V_{\mathbb R}(I_y)=\operatorname{supp}\mu\).

notation.meaning: Ideal obtained from the flat moment kernel.
Real variety of the kernel ideal.

knowledge_statements.title: Unique Atomic Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness of the finite atomic measure determined by a positive flat truncation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le2t}\) be real and satisfy \(M_t(y)\succeq0\) together with \(\operatorname{rank}M_t(y)=\operatorname{rank}M_{t-1}(y)=r\). Then there exists exactly one positive Borel measure representing \(y\) through degree \(2t\). This measure is \(r\)-atomic: \(\mu=\sum_{i=1}^{r}w_i\delta_{x^{(i)}}\), with pairwise distinct points and uniquely determined positive weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive flat moment truncation determines one and only one representing measure, having exactly as many atoms as the stable rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\) has a unique positive representing measure, and that measure has exactly \(r\) atoms.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique Atomic Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete nonuniqueness of atomic measures when a truncation lacks sufficient flat information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the univariate degree-two sequence \(y_0=1\), \(y_1=0\), and \(y_2=1\). Both \(\mu_1=\tfrac12\delta_{-1}+\tfrac12\delta_1\) and \(\mu_2=\tfrac14\delta_{-\sqrt2}+\tfrac12\delta_0+\tfrac14\delta_{\sqrt2}\) represent these moments, yet their supports and cardinalities differ. Thus positivity of the truncated moment matrix alone does not ensure uniqueness of an atomic representing measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The same mass, mean, and second moment can arise from distinct two- and three-atomic measures, so positivity alone gives no uniqueness.
assumptions_latex: \(y=(1,0,1)\) is interpreted as moments through degree two.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mu_1\ne\mu_2\) but \(\int x^k\,d\mu_1=\int x^k\,d\mu_2=y_k\) for \(k=0,1,2\).

notation.meaning: Two distinct positive atomic representing measures.

Without this equality, uniqueness cannot be inferred from \(M_t(y)\succeq0\) alone: distinct positive atomic measures can agree on every polynomial of degree at most \(2t\). Other independent determinacy conditions may nevertheless establish uniqueness in particular nonflat cases.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplication-Matrix Extraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of flat-measure atoms and weights from quotient-algebra multiplication operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a positive flat moment matrix of rank \(r\). Choose monomials \(B=(b_1,\ldots,b_r)\) whose principal matrix \(M_B\) is nonsingular. For each coordinate \(x_j\), form \(M_{B,x_jB}=(L_y(b_ax_jb_b))_{a,b}\) and solve \(M_BX_j=M_{B,x_jB}\). Jointly diagonalize the commuting matrices \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\); their joint eigenvalue tuples are the atoms \(x^{(i)}\). Solve \(y_\alpha=\sum_iw_i(x^{(i)})^\alpha\) for the weights. Output the atoms and positive weights when the moment residual is zero within the prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build coordinate multiplication matrices, jointly diagonalize them to obtain atoms, then solve the moment equations for their weights.
assumptions_latex: The supplied moment matrix is positive and flat with rank \(r\).
The selected basis matrix \(M_B\) is nonsingular.
The required shifted moments are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(\{(w_i,x^{(i)})\}_{i=1}^r\) reconstructs the flat truncated moments.

notation.meaning: Selected quotient-algebra monomial basis.
Matrix representing multiplication by coordinate x_j.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an exact positive flat moment matrix \(M_t(y)\). Compute a basis \(c^{(1)},\ldots,c^{(s)}\) of \(\ker M_t(y)\), and convert each vector to \(p_\ell(x)=\sum_{|\alpha|\le t}c^{(\ell)}_\alpha x^\alpha\). Choose a monomial basis of the column space, use the flat column relations to reduce each admissible border monomial to that basis, and collect the resulting border polynomials. Form the zero-dimensional ideal \(I_y\) generated by these reduced relations, compute a reduced generating set, and solve its real zero set. Output the kernel polynomials, generators of \(I_y\), and \(V_{\mathbb R}(I_y)\); under flatness this real zero set equals the atomic support.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute exact nullspace polynomials, use flat border relations to generate the kernel ideal, and solve its real zero set to recover the atomic support.

children.top_down_role: Recovery of polynomial ideals associated with atomic supports.

assumptions_latex: \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le 2d}\) is a truncated moment sequence with \(M_d(y)\succeq0\).
\(y\) has a flat extension and represents an \(r\)-atomic measure supported on \(S=\{x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(r)}\}\subset\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I_{\mathrm{ext}}\subseteq I(S)\), and equality holds when the kernel polynomials generate \(I(S)\).

Real vanishing ideal of the atomic support.

auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Flat finite-atomic case; equality requires a kernel basis generating the full support ideal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute a basis \(p_1,\ldots,p_s\) of \(\ker M_d(y)\), interpreting each coefficient vector as a polynomial of degree at most \(d\), and form \[ I_{\mathrm{ext}}=\langle p_1,\ldots,p_s\rangle\subset\mathbb R[x]. \] For every atom \(x^{(i)}\in S\) and every \(p\in\ker M_d(y)\), positivity gives \(p(x^{(i)})=0\); hence \(I_{\mathrm{ext}}\subseteq I(S)\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Truncated correspondence under flatness and unique finite-atomic representability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p\in\mathbb R[x]_{\le d}\), the atomic factorization of the moment matrix yields \[ p^{\mathsf T}M_d(y)p=\sum_{i=1}^r w_i p(x^{(i)})^2,\qquad w_i>0. \] Consequently, \(p\in\ker M_d(y)\) if and only if \(p(x^{(i)})=0\) for every \(i\), so \[ \ker M_d(y)=I(S)\cap\mathbb R[x]_{\le d}. \] Moreover, if \(p\in\ker M_d(y)\) and \(q\in\mathbb R[x]\) satisfies \(\deg(pq)\le d\), then \(pq\in\ker M_d(y)\). Thus the kernel is a degree-truncated ideal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under flatness, the moment-matrix kernel consists exactly of bounded-degree polynomials vanishing on the atomic support and is closed under degree-admissible multiplication.

assumptions_latex: \(y\) has a flat \(r\)-atomic representing measure \(\sum_{i=1}^r w_i\delta_{x^{(i)}}\) with distinct atoms.
A monomial basis \(B\) of the \(r\)-dimensional quotient induced by \(\operatorname{col}M_d(y)\) is available.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic support recovery from commuting multiplication matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each coordinate \(x_j\), reduce every product \(x_jb\), \(b\in B\), modulo the moment-kernel relations and place its coefficients in the multiplication matrix \(X_j\). The matrices \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) commute and are simultaneously diagonalizable in the radical finite-support case. Compute common eigenvectors \(v_i\) and record \[ x^{(i)}=\bigl(\lambda_{i1},\ldots,\lambda_{in}\bigr),\qquad X_jv_i=\lambda_{ij}v_i. \] The output support is \(S=\{x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(r)}\}\), equal to the support of the representing measure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weight recovery after exact support extraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form \(m_B=(L_y(b_1),\ldots,L_y(b_r))^{\mathsf T}\) and the square evaluation matrix \(V\) with entries \(V_{ki}=b_k(x^{(i)})\). Solve \[ Vw=m_B. \] Since \(V\) is nonsingular, this system has the unique solution \(w=V^{-1}m_B\). For the positive flat representing measure, the recovered entries obey \(w_i>0\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^r w_i=y_0\). The output measure is \(\mu=\sum_{i=1}^r w_i\delta_{x^{(i)}}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local perturbation diagnostics for weights and simple separated support eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If only the moment vector is perturbed, then the recovered weight perturbation satisfies \[ \frac{\|\delta w\|}{\|w\|}\le \kappa(V)\frac{\|\delta m_B\|}{\|m_B\|}. \] For the separating multiplication matrix, every eigenvalue \(\widetilde\lambda\) of \(X+E\) lies within \(\kappa(Q)\|E\|\) of some eigenvalue of \(X\). If \(2\kappa(Q)\|E\|<\operatorname{sep}(\Lambda)\), the eigenvalues can be matched uniquely to the atoms. Thus nearly singular \(V\), ill-conditioned \(Q\), or clustered eigenvalues make atomic recovery unstable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weight recovery deteriorates with the evaluation matrix condition number; support recovery deteriorates when eigenvectors are ill-conditioned or atom-separating eigenvalues are clustered.
knowledge_statements.title: Recovery Conditioning

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\{x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(r)}\}\) be the support of \(\mu\). Under the stated assumptions, \[S\subseteq\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in K}f(x).\] Equivalently, \(f(x^{(i)})=f^*\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If an exact flat optimal moment solution has a feasible representing measure with strictly positive atomic weights, every extracted atom is a global minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in\mathbb R[x]\) is minimized on a basic closed set \(K\), with finite optimum \(f^*\).
An optimal relaxation sequence \(y\) has a flat representing measure \(\mu=\sum_{i=1}^r w_i\delta_{x^{(i)}}\) supported on \(K\).

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrange-Multiplier Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted polynomial KKT moment hierarchy; no claim of convergence to the original optimum without appropriate compactness and constraint-qualification assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Introduce lifted variables \(z=(x,\lambda,\mu)\) and the polynomial KKT system \[F_{\mathrm{KKT}}=\left\{
abla f(x)-\sum_i\lambda_i
abla h_i(x)-\sum_j\mu_j
abla g_j(x),\ h_i(x),\ \mu_jg_j(x)ight\}.\] At order \(d\), use a truncated moment sequence \(y\) in the variables \(z\), minimize \(L_y(f)\), and impose \(y_0=1\), \(M_d(y)\succeq0\), degree-admissible equality moment constraints for every component of \(F_{\mathrm{KKT}}\), and positive-semidefinite localizing matrices for \(g_j(x)\) and \(\mu_j\). The resulting value is the order-\(d\) relaxation value for the lifted KKT problem. If a flat feasible sequence has a representing measure, its atoms yield lifted KKT points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lift the variables by adding equality and inequality multipliers, then impose truncated moment conditions for stationarity, feasibility, complementarity, and nonnegative inequality multipliers. Flat representable solutions can be used to extract KKT points.
assumptions_latex: Multiplier variables \(\lambda_i\) and \(\mu_j\) are introduced, with \(\mu_j\ge0\).
All moment and localizing constraints are included only when their degrees are admissible at relaxation order \(d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The order-\(d\) hierarchy is a truncated moment relaxation of the lifted polynomial KKT problem; flat representable solutions permit extraction of lifted KKT points.

notation.meaning: Lifted vector of primal variables and KKT multipliers.
Lifted polynomial KKT equations.
Riesz functional of the lifted truncated moment sequence.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: polynomial KKT equations can be imposed through moment and localizing constraints

assumptions_latex: All terms in each relaxation are truncated to degree at most \(2d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The order-\(d\) gradient-ideal bound is \(\rho_d=\sup\{\gamma:f-\gamma\in\Sigma[x]_{2d}+I_{\nabla f,2d}\}\).

notation.meaning: Ideal generated by the partial derivatives of \(f\).
Sums of squares of degree at most \(2d\).
Order-\(d\) certified lower bound.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: unconstrained minimizers satisfy gradient equations and SOS certificates may be taken modulo the gradient ideal
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained gradient-ideal SOS hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_{\nabla f}=\langle \partial f/\partial x_1,\ldots,\partial f/\partial x_n\rangle\), and let \(I_{\nabla f,2d}\) denote its degree-\(2d\) truncation. The order-\(d\) relaxation is \[ \rho_d=\sup_{\gamma\in\mathbb R}\left\{\gamma: f-\gamma=\sigma+\sum_{i=1}^n q_i\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i},\ \sigma\in\Sigma[x],\ \deg\sigma\le2d,\ \deg\left(q_i\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i}\right)\le2d\right\}. \] Its moment dual imposes vanishing localizing constraints for all gradient generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certify lower bounds by expressing the objective gap as a sum of squares modulo the ideal generated by the objective's partial derivatives.
knowledge_statements.title: Gradient-Ideal Hierarchies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The SOS representation modulo the truncated gradient ideal is internally consistent and the representation kind is suitable, but no authoritative gradient-hierarchy source with a locator is cited.

knowledge_statements.title: Jacobian Moment Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth equality-constrained Jacobian moment hierarchy; inequality-active-set and singular variants are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Form \[J_f(x)=[
abla f(x)\ 
abla h_1(x)\ \cdots\ 
abla h_m(x)]\] and let \(\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_s\) be its \((m+1)	imes(m+1)\) minors. Under the full-rank assumption, a point \(x\in V(h)\) is first-order stationary exactly when \(\phi_\ell(x)=0\) for every \(\ell\). At each relaxation order, the Jacobian moment hierarchy imposes degree-admissible equality moment or localizing constraints for all \(h_i\) and \(\phi_\ell\), together with the moment-matrix positivity constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For smooth equality constraints, form the maximal minors of the objective-constraint Jacobian and add their vanishing constraints, together with the original equalities, to each admissible moment relaxation.
assumptions_latex: The equality-feasible set \(V(h)\) is smooth: \(\operatorname{rank}[\nabla h_1(x)\ \cdots\ \nabla h_m(x)]=m\) for every \(x\in V(h)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On \(V(h)\), the equations \(\phi_\ell=0\) characterize first-order stationarity, and adjoining their degree-admissible moment constraints defines the smooth equality-constrained Jacobian moment hierarchy.

notation.meaning: Jacobian matrix containing the objective and equality-constraint gradients.
The maximal minors of \(J_f\).
Equality-feasible real variety.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: maximal Jacobian minors eliminate equality multipliers under full constraint rank

knowledge_statements.title: Preordering-Refined Tight Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence for compact basic closed sets using the full preordering generated by the stated inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a compact basic closed feasible set, lower bounds obtained from successive degree truncations of the full inequality preordering are monotone and converge to the global minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The truncated-preordering bounds satisfy \(\rho_d\uparrow f^*\).

notation.meaning: Preordering generated by the inequality polynomials.
Degree-\(2d\) truncation of the preordering.
Order-\(d\) certified lower bound.
