children.title: Correlative-Sparsity Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Variable-interaction decompositions and consistency across local moment models.

assumptions_latex: Variable cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_p\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) cover the supports of all objective and constraint polynomials.
Each polynomial is assigned to a clique containing all variables on which it depends.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sparse relaxation consists of clique-local moment and localizing constraints coupled by equality of overlap moments.

notation.meaning: Moment sequence indexed only by variables in clique \(C_k\).
Clique-local moment matrix.
Intersection of two variable cliques.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: correlative-sparse relaxations replace a global moment matrix by coupled clique-local matrices
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correlative-sparsity model with explicit overlap consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At order \(d\), introduce one truncated sequence \(y^{(k)}\) for each clique \(C_k\). Impose \(M_d^{C_k}(y^{(k)})\succeq0\) and, for every constraint \(g_j\) assigned to \(C_k\), impose its clique-local positive-semidefinite localizing matrix. If \(\alpha\) is supported in \(C_k\cap C_\ell\) and \(|\alpha|\le2d\), require \[ y^{(k)}_\alpha=y^{(\ell)}_\alpha. \] Apply each clique-local Riesz functional to its assigned objective terms and minimize their sum, with the common zeroth moment normalized to one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace the global moment sequence by one sequence per variable clique, impose local positivity, and equate all moments visible on clique overlaps.
knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Local Moment Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition accurately describes coupled clique-local moment models and fits the terminal container, but no sparse-moment reference with a specific locator is supplied.

assumptions_latex: \(C_1,\ldots,C_p\) are variable cliques in a fixed ordering.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ordering has the running-intersection property exactly when \(C_k\cap\bigcup_{i<k}C_i\subseteq C_{j(k)}\) for every \(k\ge2\).

notation.meaning: Ordered variable cliques.
A preceding clique covering the earlier-variable overlap of \(C_k\).

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: running intersection is the standard clique-ordering condition used to glue consistent local data
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordered-clique form of the running-intersection property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An ordering \(C_1,\ldots,C_p\) satisfies the running-intersection property if, for each \(k=2,\ldots,p\), there exists an index \(j(k)<k\) such that \[ C_k\cap\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^{k-1}C_i\right)\subseteq C_{j(k)}. \] Equivalently, each clique's variables already seen in earlier cliques are all contained together in one earlier clique. This condition supplies a clique-tree attachment \(C_k\to C_{j(k)}\) along which overlap consistency can be imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each clique's overlap with all earlier cliques must be contained in one earlier clique, yielding a tree-compatible organization of local moment models.
knowledge_statements.title: Running-Intersection Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ordered-clique running-intersection condition is precise, internally consistent, and correctly classified as a condition, but it lacks an authoritative citation with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Measure Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency condition for clique-local measures in a correlative-sparsity relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_1,\ldots,I_p\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and let \(\mu_k\) be a finite Borel measure on \(\mathbb R^{I_k}\). The family \((\mu_k)_{k=1}^p\) is locally consistent through degree \(2d\) when, for every \(k,\ell\) and every multi-index \(\alpha\in\mathbb N^{I_k\cap I_\ell}\) with \(|\alpha|\le 2d\), \[\int x^\alpha\,d\mu_k=\int x^\alpha\,d\mu_\ell.\] Full local consistency requires equality of the pushforward marginals \((\pi_{I_k\cap I_\ell})_\#\mu_k=(\pi_{I_k\cap I_\ell})_\#\mu_\ell\) on every overlap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clique-local measures are consistent when their marginals, or all retained overlap moments, agree on every pairwise variable intersection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\mu_k)_{k=1}^p\) has matching overlap moments through degree \(2d\), with full consistency characterized by equal overlap marginals.

notation.meaning: coordinate projection onto variables indexed by J
pushforward marginal of measure μ under the projection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the terminal container and is internally coherent, but no citation supports the choice between truncated overlap-moment consistency and equality of full marginals. An authoritative source with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Term-Sparsity Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Monomial-support and sparse matrix-pattern reductions.

knowledge_statements.title: Monomial-Support Decompositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block decomposition induced by the monomial interaction graph at a fixed relaxation order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a monomial basis \(B_d=\{x^\alpha:|\alpha|\le d\}\) and a support set \(S\subseteq\mathbb N^n\). Form the graph \(G_d(S)\) on \(B_d\), joining \(x^\alpha\) and \(x^\beta\) whenever \(\alpha+\beta\in S\). If its connected components are \(C_1,\ldots,C_q\), then every symmetric Gram matrix \(Q\) satisfying \(Q_{\alpha\beta}=0\) across distinct components decomposes as \[Q=Q[C_1]\oplus\cdots\oplus Q[C_q].\] Consequently, \(Q\succeq0\) is equivalent to \(Q[C_r]\succeq0\) for every \(r\), yielding componentwise moment or Gram constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graph on retained monomials partitions a sparse moment or Gram matrix into independent positive-semidefinite blocks.
assumptions_latex: Entries connecting distinct graph components are constrained to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sparse positive-semidefinite constraint decomposes into one positive-semidefinite constraint per connected component.

notation.meaning: monomial basis through degree d
monomial interaction graph induced by support S
principal submatrix indexed by component C

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The block decomposition is valid for the explicitly zeroed cross-component entries, but the stated support graph is only one possible term-sparsity construction. A source must verify that this graph and its resulting moment/Gram interpretation match the intended hierarchy.

knowledge_statements.title: Term-Sparsity Completion Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative chordal-completion construction for term-sparse moment or Gram relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given relaxation degree \(d\), initial exponent support \(S_0\), and monomial basis \(B_d\), set \(t=0\). Construct \(G_t\) on \(B_d\) with edge \(\{\alpha,\beta\}\) whenever \(\alpha+\beta\in S_t\); choose a chordal extension \(\widehat G_t\), impose positive semidefiniteness on every maximal-clique principal submatrix, and update \[S_{t+1}=S_t\cup\{\alpha+\beta:\{\alpha,\beta\}\in E(\widehat G_t)\}.\] Stop when \(S_{t+1}=S_t\), or after a prescribed number of completions, and output the resulting sparse semidefinite relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated support extension and chordal completion produce increasingly coupled term-sparse semidefinite relaxations until stabilization or a chosen iteration limit.
assumptions_latex: A chordal extension is selected at each iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a nested support-completion hierarchy of clique-wise positive-semidefinite relaxations.

notation.meaning: term-interaction graph at completion step t
chosen chordal extension of the interaction graph

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf, but term-sparsity completion schemes differ in support extension, chordal completion, and localizing-matrix treatment. No source establishes that the displayed update produces the claimed nested hierarchy.

knowledge_statements.title: Correlative–Term Sparsity Hybrids
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-level sparse representation combining variable cliques with monomial graphs inside each clique.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_1,\ldots,I_p\) be variable cliques covering every monomial of the objective and constraints. For each \(k\), choose a local monomial basis \(B_{k,d}\subseteq\mathbb R[x_{I_k}]\) and a chordal term graph with maximal cliques \(C_{k,1},\ldots,C_{k,q_k}\). The hybrid order-\(d\) relaxation replaces the dense moment condition by \[M_d(y)[C_{k,r}]\succeq0\quad(k=1,\ldots,p;\ r=1,\ldots,q_k),\] together with analogous localizing blocks and equality of all retained moments shared by overlapping variable cliques.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The hybrid first splits variables into correlative cliques, then splits each clique's moment matrices by monomial interactions while matching shared moments.
assumptions_latex: Every polynomial support is contained in at least one variable clique.
Each local term graph is supplied with a chordal extension.
Shared retained moments use a common indexing convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxation consists of term-sparse positive-semidefinite blocks nested within correlative-sparsity cliques, coupled by overlap equalities.

notation.meaning: degree-d local monomial basis for variable clique k
maximal monomial clique r within variable clique k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-level representation matches the title, but the precise hybrid construction, localizing-block indices, completion rule, and overlap equalities are method-dependent and unsupported by a cited source.

children.title: Symmetry-Adapted Moment Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Invariant coordinate systems and representation-theoretic block reductions.

knowledge_statements.title: Invariant Moment Coordinates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment coordinates restricted to the invariant polynomial subspace of a finite symmetry group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite group \(G\) act linearly on \(\mathbb R^n\), and assume the feasible set and objective are \(G\)-invariant. For any truncated moment functional \(L_y\), define its symmetrization by \[L_{\bar y}(p)=\frac{1}{|G|}\sum_{g\in G}L_y(p\circ g).\] Then \(L_{\bar y}(p)=L_y(\mathcal R_Gp)\), where \(\mathcal R_Gp=|G|^{-1}\sum_{g\in G}p\circ g\), and \(L_{\bar y}(p\circ g)=L_{\bar y}(p)\). Thus the symmetrized relaxation is parameterized by moments of a basis of \(\mathbb R[x]^G\) through the truncation degree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaging a moment functional over the symmetry group makes it invariant, so only coordinates dual to invariant polynomials are needed.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite group acting linearly on \(\mathbb R^n\).
The optimization data are invariant under the action.
All displayed polynomials lie within the chosen truncation degree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The averaged moment functional is \(G\)-invariant and admits coordinates indexed by a truncated basis of \(\mathbb R[x]^G\).

notation.meaning: Reynolds averaging operator
ring of polynomials invariant under G

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Finite-group averaging and invariance are standard, and the representation fits the leaf. A source is still required to support the stronger claim that the symmetry-reduced moment relaxation can be parameterized solely by the stated truncated invariant-polynomial coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry Block Diagonalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Isotypic block decomposition of invariant moment matrices under a finite orthogonal group action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) act orthogonally on the finite-dimensional polynomial space \(V_d\), and let \(M\) be a symmetric moment or localizing matrix satisfying \(\rho(g)^\top M\rho(g)=M\) for every \(g\in G\). Decompose \(V_d\) into real isotypic components. There exists an orthogonal symmetry-adapted basis \(U\) such that \[U^\top MU=\bigoplus_{\lambda}M_\lambda,\] with blocks indexed by real irreducible representation types, including their multiplicities. Hence \(M\succeq0\) if and only if \(M_\lambda\succeq0\) for every \(\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A group-invariant moment matrix becomes block diagonal in a symmetry-adapted basis, and positivity can be checked block by block.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and acts orthogonally on \(V_d\).
\(M\) commutes with the induced group representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An orthogonal basis block-diagonalizes \(M\) by isotypic type, reducing positive semidefiniteness to its symmetry blocks.

notation.meaning: representation of G on the truncated polynomial space
matrix block associated with an isotypic representation type

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role is appropriate, but real isotypic decompositions can involve multiplicity spaces and real, complex, or quaternionic commutants. A specific source is needed to confirm that the stated block description is sufficiently precise for the intended moment-matrix reduction.

children.title: Multi-Ordered Moment Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Relaxations using nonuniform orders across constraints or variable blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Specific Relaxation Orders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility conditions for assigning distinct localizing orders to individual polynomial constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), assign constraint \(j\) an integer order \(r_j\) satisfying \(r_j\ge\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil\). A truncated sequence \(y=(y_\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le2d}\) supports these orders when \(d\ge\max_j r_j\), \(M_d(y)\succeq0\), and \[M_{r_j-\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil}(g_jy)\succeq0\quad(j=1,\ldots,m).\] Increasing any \(r_j\) adds only the corresponding higher-degree localizing conditions, provided the required moments are present.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each constraint may receive its own order, but that order must cover half its degree and all required localizing moments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed degree and positive-semidefiniteness conditions define a valid constraint-specific multi-order relaxation.

notation.meaning: moment matrix of order d
localizing matrix of order s for constraint polynomial g_j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but the meaning of the constraint order and the formula M_{r_j-ceil(deg(g_j)/2)}(g_j y) are convention-dependent. A source must confirm this indexing and the claim about independently increasing a constraint order.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Specific Relaxation Orders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinct moment orders assigned to variable or sparsity blocks with consistent shared truncations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_1,\ldots,I_p\) be variable blocks and assign block \(k\) an order \(d_k\). For every constraint \(g_j\) assigned to block \(k\), require \(\operatorname{supp}(g_j)\subseteq\mathbb N^{I_k}\) and \(d_k\ge\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil\). The blockwise relaxation imposes \(M_{d_k}(y^{(k)})\succeq0\) and all admissible localizing constraints in block \(k\). On an overlap \(I_k\cap I_\ell\), it equates moments through degree \[2\min(d_k,d_\ell).\] These conditions define compatible unequal-order local moment models.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable blocks can use different orders when each covers its assigned constraints and overlapping blocks agree through their common available degree.
assumptions_latex: Each assigned constraint uses variables from its block.
Each local sequence \(y^{(k)}\) is available through degree \(2d_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The local moment models are degree-valid and mutually consistent through the maximum degree shared by each block pair.

notation.meaning: variable index set of block k
relaxation order assigned to block k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed condition is plausible, but no source supports the block-assignment model or the requirement to match every overlap moment through degree 2 min(d_k,d_l). These choices can depend on the sparse hierarchy and running-intersection construction.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Relaxation-Order Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-driven update rule for a multi-ordered moment relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize admissible orders \(r^{(0)}=(r_1^{(0)},\ldots,r_m^{(0)})\) and solve the corresponding relaxation. At iteration \(t\), compute nonnegative indicators \(\eta_j^{(t)}\) measuring the unresolved contribution or violation associated with constraint \(j\). Choose \(J_t\subseteq\{j:\eta_j^{(t)}\ge\tau_t\}\), update \[r_j^{(t+1)}=r_j^{(t)}+1\quad(j\in J_t),\qquad r_j^{(t+1)}=r_j^{(t)}\quad(j\notin J_t),\] rebuild the affected moment and localizing blocks, and stop when the certified gap and all indicators meet prescribed tolerances or a resource limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve, score constraints or blocks, raise orders only where indicators are large, and stop at certified tolerances or a resource limit.
assumptions_latex: Initial orders satisfy all degree requirements.
Each indicator \(\eta_j^{(t)}\) is computable from the current relaxation.
Stopping tolerances and a resource limit are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm outputs a feasible multi-order assignment and its relaxation solution at the selected stopping iteration.

notation.meaning: order of constraint j at iteration t
adaptive refinement indicator
set of constraints refined at iteration t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the adaptive-selection leaf, but the indicators and certified gap are not mathematically defined, and no fairness or exhaustive-refinement condition is given. A method-specific source is required before the algorithm and its stopping claim are reliable.

children.title: Real-Complex Moment Hierarchy Pair
children.top_down_role: Real symmetric and complex Hermitian moment formulations and their exactness regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Real Moment-SOS Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-d primal moment relaxation and dual truncated quadratic-module bound over real variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f,g_j\in\mathbb R[x]\) and \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\ge0\}\), let \(s_j=\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil\) and set \(g_0=1\). At order \(d\ge\max_j s_j\), the real moment bound is \[\inf_y\ L_y(f)\quad\text{subject to}\quad y_0=1,\quad M_{d-s_j}(g_jy)\succeq0\quad(j=0,\ldots,m).\] Its SOS dual is \[\sup_\gamma\ \gamma\quad\text{subject to}\quad f-\gamma=\sum_{j=0}^m\sigma_jg_j,\quad \sigma_j\text{ SOS},\quad\deg(\sigma_jg_j)\le2d.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The real hierarchy pairs positive-semidefinite moment and localizing matrices with bounded-degree sums-of-squares certificates for objective lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal and dual programs give order-\(d\) moment and SOS lower bounds for minimizing \(f\) over \(K\).

notation.meaning: linear functional represented by the truncated real moment sequence y
real localizing matrix of order s
sum-of-squares multiplier

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed real moment and SOS programs are standard in form, but L_y(f) requires deg(f) <= 2d, which is not assumed. Moreover, calling the programs a dual pair requires a sourced finite-dimensional conic formulation even though equality of optimal values is not asserted.

knowledge_statements.title: Complex Moment-HSOS Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bidegree-d complex moment relaxation and dual Hermitian-sum-of-squares bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,g_j\in\mathbb C[z,\bar z]\) be real-valued Hermitian polynomials and \(K=\{z\in\mathbb C^n:g_j(z,\bar z)\ge0\}\). For a complex moment sequence \(y_{\alpha,\beta}=\overline{y_{\beta,\alpha}}\), the order-\(d\) relaxation imposes \[y_{0,0}=1,\qquad M_d^{\mathbb C}(y)\succeq0,\qquad M_{d-k_j}^{\mathbb C}(g_jy)\succeq0,\] where \(k_j\) bounds both holomorphic and antiholomorphic degrees of \(g_j\). Its dual requires \(f-\gamma=\sigma_0+\sum_j\sigma_jg_j\), where each \(\sigma_j\) is a Hermitian sum of squared moduli with compatible bidegree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The complex hierarchy uses Hermitian moment and localizing matrices, dual to bounded-bidegree sums of squared moduli certificates.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f,g_j\) is Hermitian and real-valued on \(\mathbb C^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal Hermitian moment program and dual HSOS program provide order-\(d\) lower bounds on \(\min_{z\in K}f(z,\bar z)\).

notation.meaning: Hermitian complex moment matrix
maximum holomorphic or antiholomorphic degree required by g_j
Hermitian sum of squared moduli

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The duality role fits the leaf, but the definition of k_j, the localizing index, the truncation required for f, and the compatible HSOS bidegrees are not specified precisely enough to determine the programs. These conventions require an authoritative source.

knowledge_statements.title: Complex-Hierarchy Exactness Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Flat-extension certificate for finite exactness and optimizer extraction in a complex moment relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y\) be optimal for an order-\(d\) complex moment relaxation and feasible for all Hermitian localizing constraints. If, for some \(t<d\), \[\operatorname{rank}M_d^{\mathbb C}(y)=\operatorname{rank}M_t^{\mathbb C}(y)=r,\] and the truncation satisfies the applicable complex flat-extension hypotheses, then \(y\) has a representing measure \(\mu=\sum_{i=1}^r w_i\delta_{z^{(i)}}\) supported on the feasible set, with \(w_i>0\). Consequently, the relaxation value equals the global optimum, and every support point attaining the represented objective value is a global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible optimal complex moment sequence with a valid rank-stable flat extension yields a finite atomic feasible measure and certifies exactness.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(n\) variables and relaxation order \(r\), a dense total-degree monomial basis contains one monomial \(x^\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^n_r\). Its cardinality is
\[
s(n,r)=\left|\mathbb{N}^n_r\right|=\binom{n+r}{r}.
\]
Consequently, for fixed \(n\), \(s(n,r)=\Theta(r^n)\) as \(r\to\infty\); for fixed \(r\), \(s(n,r)=\Theta(n^r)\) as \(n\to\infty\). Thus even before semidefinite blocks are formed, dense coefficient and basis-index storage grows combinatorially in the joint parameters \(n\) and \(r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The total-degree basis through order r has binomial(n+r,r) monomials, growing polynomially in either parameter separately but combinatorially when dimension and order increase together.
knowledge_statements.title: Monomial-Basis Growth

M_r(y)\in\mathbb{S}^{s(n,r)},\qquad s(n,r)=\binom{n+r}{r}.

knowledge_statements.title: Localizing-Block Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One dense localizing block for a polynomial inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), let \(g(x)=\sum_\gamma g_\gamma x^\gamma\in\mathbb{R}[x]\) have degree \(d_g\), and set \(t_g=\lceil d_g/2\rceil\). For an integer \(r\ge t_g\) and a truncated sequence \(y=(y_\delta)_{|\delta|\le 2r}\), the order-\(r\) localizing block is indexed by \(\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{N}^n_{r-t_g}\), with entries
\[
(M_{r-t_g}(g y))_{\alpha,\beta}=\sum_\gamma g_\gamma y_{\alpha+\beta+\gamma}.
\]
Its matrix dimension is \(s(n,r-t_g)=\binom{n+r-t_g}{r-t_g}\). For inequalities \(g_j(x)\ge0\), a dense relaxation contains one such positive-semidefinite block for each included inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In n variables, a degree-d constraint at relaxation order r contributes a localizing block of dimension binomial(n+r-ceil(d/2),r-ceil(d/2)); included inequalities contribute separate blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Monomial-Basis Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate representation of dense moment and localizing matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), \(v_r(x)=(x^\alpha)_{|\alpha|\le r}\), and \(y=(y_\gamma)_{|\gamma|\le 2r}\). Define the truncated Riesz functional by \(L_y(x^\gamma)=y_\gamma\) and extend it linearly. The moment matrix in the total-degree monomial basis is
\[
M_r(y)=L_y\!\left(v_r(x)v_r(x)^{\mathsf T}\right),
\]
where \(L_y\) acts entrywise, so \((M_r(y))_{\alpha,\beta}=y_{\alpha+\beta}\). If \(g\in\mathbb{R}[x]\) and \(s\ge0\) satisfies \(2s+\deg(g)\le2r\), its localizing matrix is \(L_y(gv_s v_s^{\mathsf T})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Applying the truncated moment functional entrywise to a monomial outer product produces the moment matrix; inserting a polynomial at an order compatible with the truncation produces its localizing matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_r(y)=L_y(v_rv_r^{\mathsf T})\), with \((M_r(y))_{\alpha,\beta}=y_{\alpha+\beta}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q_r(x)=(q_\alpha(x))_{|\alpha|\le r}\) be a basis, commonly orthogonal with respect to a selected reference measure, and suppose \(q_r=T_rv_r\) with \(T_r\) invertible. Its moment Gram matrix satisfies
\[
G_r^{q}(y):=L_y(q_rq_r^{\mathsf T})=T_rM_r(y)T_r^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Therefore \(G_r^{q}(y)\succeq0\) if and only if \(M_r(y)\succeq0\). Localizing matrices transform by the same congruence at their respective orders. The basis change preserves the exact relaxation feasible set after consistent coefficient transformation, although its numerical conditioning depends on the reference measure and scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible orthogonal-polynomial basis change congruently transforms moment and localizing matrices, preserving exact semidefinite feasibility while potentially changing numerical conditioning.

For \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), choose \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and invertible diagonal \(D\), and substitute \(x=c+Dz\). Define \(\widetilde f(z)=f(c+Dz)\) and \(\widetilde g_j(z)=g_j(c+Dz)\). Then
\[
\inf_{x\in K}f(x)=\inf_{z\in D^{-1}(K-c)}\widetilde f(z),
\qquad D^{-1}(K-c)=\{z:\widetilde g_j(z)\ge0\}.
\]
Because affine substitution preserves polynomial degree and sums of squares, consistently transformed moment or SOS relaxations represent the same exact polynomial optimization problem in different coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible affine variable scaling gives an equivalent polynomial optimization problem and preserves degrees and sums of squares under consistent substitution.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive scalar normalization of polynomial inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), where \(g_j\in\mathbb{R}[x]\), and choose \(a_j>0\). Replacing \(g_j(x)\ge0\) by \(a_jg_j(x)\ge0\) leaves \(K\) unchanged. For every integer \(s\ge0\) and every real sequence \(y\) containing the moments required by the localizing matrix,
\[
M_s(a_jg_jy)=a_jM_s(g_jy).
\]
Thus \(M_s(a_jg_jy)\succeq0\) is equivalent in exact arithmetic to \(M_s(g_jy)\succeq0\). Positive constraint scaling preserves the corresponding finite relaxation feasible set and objective value when applied consistently; zero or negative factors do not have this equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplying an inequality by a positive scalar preserves its feasible set and scales every well-defined localizing block without changing exact relaxation values.
assumptions_latex: \(s\in\mathbb{N}\) and \(y\) contains all moments needed for \(M_s(g_jy)\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K=\{x:a_jg_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(M_s(a_jg_jy)=a_jM_s(g_jy)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Scaling Interactions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistent simultaneous scaling of variables, constraints, moments, and dual multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}\), apply the invertible affine substitution \(x=c+Dz\), and replace each transformed constraint by \(a_j(S_{c,D}g_j)(z)\ge0\), where \(a_j>0\) and \((S_{c,D}p)(z)=p(c+Dz)\). For every admissible localizing order \(s\) and transformed moment sequence \(\widetilde y\),
\[
M_s(a_jS_{c,D}g_j\,\widetilde y)=a_jM_s(S_{c,D}g_j\,\widetilde y).
\]
The affine substitution induces an invertible linear correspondence between the relevant truncated moment functionals, and the factor \(a_j\) is compensated by the corresponding dual SOS multiplier. Consequently, consistent joint scaling preserves exact primal and dual relaxation values. Its numerical effect is model-dependent because variable scaling changes coefficients and moment coordinates while constraint scaling changes block magnitudes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invertible variable scaling and positive constraint scaling preserve exact primal and dual relaxations when moments, coefficients, and multipliers are transformed consistently, although their numerical effects interact.
assumptions_latex: \(s\in\mathbb{N}\) and \(\widetilde y\) contains all moments required by the displayed localizing matrices
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_s(a_j(S_{c,D}g_j)\,\widetilde y)=a_jM_s((S_{c,D}g_j)\,\widetilde y)\), with equivalent consistently transformed exact primal and dual relaxation values.

\[

knowledge_statements.title: Dual SOS-Model Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Truncated quadratic-module interface dual to the dense moment SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g_0=1\), set \(t_0=0\), and define \(t_j=\lceil\deg(g_j)/2\rceil\) for \(j=1,\ldots,m\). The order-\(r\) dual SOS interface is
\[
d_r=\sup_{\lambda,\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_m}\left\{\lambda:f-\lambda=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j,\ \sigma_j\in\Sigma[x],\ \deg(\sigma_0)\le2r,\ \deg(\sigma_jg_j)\le2r\right\}.
\]
Each multiplier has a Gram representation \(\sigma_j=v_{r-t_j}^{\mathsf T}Q_jv_{r-t_j}\) with \(Q_j\succeq0\). Equating polynomial coefficients converts the identity into affine equations in \(\lambda\) and the Gram matrices, yielding an SDP representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual interface maximizes a certified lower bound whose objective gap belongs to the degree-truncated quadratic module, with every SOS multiplier represented by a degree-compatible positive-semidefinite Gram matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_r=\sup_\lambda\{\lambda:f-\lambda=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j,\ \sigma_j\in\Sigma[x],\ \deg(\sigma_0)\le2r,\ \deg(\sigma_jg_j)\le2r\}\).

children.title: Primal–Dual Interface Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Mapping between primal blocks, dual certificates, and solver outputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Interface Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional conic duality between matched moment and SOS SDP interfaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Pair each primal constraint \(M_{r-t_j}(g_jy)\succeq0\) with a dual matrix \(Q_j\succeq0\). Under matched bases, coefficient orderings, and degree truncations, the adjoint localizing and Gram maps yield the coefficient identity
\[
f-\lambda=\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j.
\]
The resulting finite-dimensional primal and dual SDPs satisfy weak duality \(d_r\le p_r\). If the primal SDP is strictly feasible and \(p_r\) is finite, then \(d_r=p_r\) and the dual optimum is attained. If the dual SDP is strictly feasible and \(d_r\) is finite, then \(d_r=p_r\) and the primal optimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matched localizing and SOS Gram maps are adjoint under coefficient matching, so weak duality always holds. Primal Slater regularity with a finite primal value gives equality and dual attainment; dual Slater regularity with a finite dual value gives equality and primal attainment.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual models use identical bases, coefficient orderings, and degree truncations.
The displayed moment and SOS programs form a finite-dimensional conic primal-dual pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_r\le p_r\); primal Slater regularity with finite \(p_r\) implies \(d_r=p_r\) and dual attainment, while dual Slater regularity with finite \(d_r\) implies \(d_r=p_r\) and primal attainment.

For \(j=0,\ldots,q\), let \(B_j(y)\in\mathbb S^{n_j}\) be a moment or localizing matrix block with affine expansion \(B_j(y)=B_{j,0}+\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_{2d}}y_\alpha B_{j,\alpha}\). A block-structured SDP interface represents the relaxation as
\[
\inf_y\ \sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_{2d}} f_\alpha y_\alpha\quad\text{subject to}\quad y_0=1,\qquad B_j(y)\succeq0\quad(j=0,\ldots,q),
\]
possibly together with additional affine equalities. Each block is exported separately, while every repeated moment refers to the same scalar variable \(y_\alpha\); consequently, the block representation preserves cross-block moment consistency.

children.title: Facial-Reduction Procedures
children.top_down_role: Reduction to smaller semidefinite faces for structurally singular moment models.

knowledge_statements.title: Facial-Reduction Procedures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact facial reduction for a semidefinite feasibility system lacking ambient strict feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(\mathcal F_0=\{X\in\mathbb S_+^n:\mathcal A(X)=b\}\), initialize \(F_0=\mathbb S_+^n\). At iteration \(k\), find \(z_k\) such that \(Z_k=\mathcal A^*z_k\in F_k^*\), \(b^\top z_k=0\), and \(Z_k\) does not vanish identically on \(F_k\). Replace
\[
F_{k+1}=F_k\cap\{X:\langle Z_k,X\rangle=0\}.
\]
Stop when the affine system has a feasible point in \(\operatorname{ri}F_k\), or when an exposing vector certifies infeasibility. Output a basis \(V\) for the final face, so feasible matrices are parameterized as \(X=VYV^\top\) with \(Y\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly expose faces containing every feasible matrix, then parameterize the final face by a smaller positive-semidefinite variable.
assumptions_latex: Each facial-reduction subproblem returns a valid exposing vector or an infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every reduction preserves \(\mathcal F_0\), and termination yields an equivalent system on a face satisfying relative strict feasibility.

notation.meaning: current face of the positive-semidefinite cone
adjoint of the constraint map
relative interior of the current face

knowledge_statements.title: Model-Regularization Strategies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Controlled perturbation of ill-conditioned semidefinite moment models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For affine constraints \(\mathcal A(X)=b\), objective \(\langle C,X\rangle\), and tolerances \(\delta>0\), \(\varepsilon\ge0\), solve the regularized model
\[
\inf_X\ \langle C,X\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|X\|_F^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad X\succeq\delta I,\qquad \|\mathcal A(X)-b\|_2\le\varepsilon.
\]
Decrease \(\delta\), \(\varepsilon\), and, when objective fidelity is required, \(\rho\) along a prescribed schedule. Stop only after reporting the original-model residual, minimum eigenvalue, and objective discrepancy; output the final iterate together with these diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularize eigenvalues, residuals, or the objective, then assess the returned point against the unperturbed SDP rather than the modified model alone.
assumptions_latex: \(C,X\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(\mathcal A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is linear.
The chosen perturbation parameters make the regularized subproblem feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is explicitly qualified by residual and perturbation errors relative to the original semidefinite model.

children.title: Reduction–Regularization Interactions
children.top_down_role: Compatibility and tradeoffs between facial reduction and model regularization.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduction–Regularization Interactions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility of exact face restriction with positive-definiteness regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose the minimal face containing the feasible matrices is
\[
F=\{VYV^\top:Y\in\mathbb S_+^r\},
\]
where \(V\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) has orthonormal columns and \(r<n\). Regularizing after facial reduction by \(Y\succeq\delta I_r\) is equivalent in ambient coordinates to \(X\succeq_F\delta VV^\top\), meaning \(X-\delta VV^\top\in F\). In contrast, imposing \(X\succeq\delta I_n\) before reduction is incompatible with every \(X\in F\) when \(\delta>0\). Thus ambient eigenvalue regularization can destroy feasibility, whereas relative-face regularization preserves the face geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-definiteness regularization must be applied inside the reduced face; an ambient identity shift makes every proper-face solution infeasible.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a proper face of \(\mathbb S_+^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Relative-face regularization is compatible with \(F\), while the constraint \(X\succeq\delta I_n\) excludes \(F\).

notation.meaning: orthonormal basis for the range defining the minimal face
positive-semidefinite order relative to the face F

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind and face-relative versus ambient comparison fit the interaction leaf, and the mathematical claim is plausible. No inspectable source is supplied for the interaction statement, so source support is required.

children.title: Numerical Flatness Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Finite-precision interpretation and validation of nearly flat moment solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Rank Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-relative numerical rank for moment matrices computed in floating-point arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\in\mathbb S_+^N\) have eigenvalues \(\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_N\ge0\). Given an absolute tolerance \(\tau_{\mathrm{abs}}\ge0\) and relative tolerance \(\tau_{\mathrm{rel}}\ge0\), define
\[
\tau(M)=\max\{\tau_{\mathrm{abs}},\tau_{\mathrm{rel}}\lambda_1\},\qquad
\operatorname{rank}_{\tau}(M)=\#\{i:\lambda_i>\tau(M)\}.
\]
The selected numerical rank is meaningful only together with the tolerances, matrix scaling, and eigenvalue gap \(\lambda_r/\max\{\lambda_{r+1},\tau_{\mathrm{abs}}\}\); changing the monomial basis or scaling can change it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Count eigenvalues above a declared absolute-relative threshold and report the separating spectral gap and scaling with the resulting numerical rank.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a computed symmetric positive-semidefinite moment matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}_{\tau}(M)\) is the tolerance-dependent numerical rank used in flatness tests.

notation.meaning: combined absolute-relative eigenvalue threshold
number of eigenvalues exceeding the threshold

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Flatness Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical surrogate for the exact flat-extension rank condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For relaxation order \(d\), let \(M_d(y)\) and \(M_{d-s}(y)\) be nested moment matrices, where \(s\) is the maximum half-degree required by the constraints. Given a common threshold rule \(\tau\), declare \(y\) near-flat only if
\[
\operatorname{rank}_{\tau}(M_d(y))=\operatorname{rank}_{\tau}(M_{d-s}(y))=r,
\]
and both matrices exhibit a reported gap between eigenvalues \(r\) and \(r+1\). The diagnostic must additionally report the normalized tail \(\sum_{i>r}\lambda_i(M_d)/\max\{\lambda_1(M_d),1\}\); near-flatness is numerical evidence, not an exact representing-measure certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested moment matrices are near-flat when their thresholded ranks agree, their spectral gaps are clear, and the discarded spectral tail is small.
assumptions_latex: \(M_{d-s}(y)\) is the principal nested moment matrix required by the applicable flat-extension theorem.
One scaling and threshold convention is used for both matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Rank agreement plus spectral separation defines a reproducible near-flatness diagnostic but does not establish exact flatness.

knowledge_statements.title: Extracted-Solution Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori validation of atoms extracted from a nearly flat moment relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let extracted atoms and weights be \((x^{(i)},w_i)_{i=1}^r\), with \(w_i\ge0\). For feasible set \(K=\{x:g_j(x)\ge0,\ h_k(x)=0\}\), define the reconstructed moments \(\widehat y_\alpha=\sum_{i=1}^r w_i(x^{(i)})^\alpha\). The extraction is validated to declared tolerances only if
\[
\left|\sum_iw_i-1\right|\le\varepsilon_m,
\quad \max_{|\alpha|\le2d}|y_\alpha-\widehat y_\alpha|\le\varepsilon_m,
\quad g_j(x^{(i)})\ge-\varepsilon_f,
\quad |h_k(x^{(i)})|\le\varepsilon_f,

children.title: Positive Semidefinite Data without a Representing Measure

knowledge_statements.title: Positive Semidefinite Data without a Representing Measure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive semidefiniteness of one truncated moment matrix is insufficient for representability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m(x,y)=x^4y^2+x^2y^4+1-3x^2y^2\), which is nonnegative on \(\mathbb R^2\) but is not a sum of squares of polynomials of degree at most three. Since the degree-six sum-of-squares cone is closed and convex, separation yields a linear functional \(L\) on \(\mathbb R[x,y]_{\le6}\) such that \(L(q^2)\ge0\) for every \(q\in\mathbb R[x,y]_{\le3}\), but \(L(m)<0\). Its truncated moment matrix \(M_3(L)\) is positive semidefinite. Nevertheless, \(L\) has no representing positive Borel measure, because any such measure would give \(L(m)=\int m\,d\mu\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separating the Motzkin polynomial from the SOS cone produces positive-semidefinite truncated moment data that cannot come from any positive measure.
assumptions_latex: Linear functionals are identified with degree-six truncated moment sequences.
A representing measure is required to be a finite positive Borel measure on \(\mathbb R^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(M_3(L)\succeq0\) whose associated truncated data have no representing positive measure.

notation.meaning: Motzkin nonnegative polynomial
separating truncated moment functional

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Incompatible Moment Data
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment data representable globally but incompatible with a prescribed semialgebraic support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the univariate data \(y_0=1\), \(y_1=0\), and \(y_2=1\). Its moment matrix is
\[
M_1(y)=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,
\]
and the data are represented on \(\mathbb R\) by \(\tfrac12\delta_{-1}+\tfrac12\delta_1\). For the required support \(K=[-\tfrac12,\tfrac12]\), however, the defining polynomial \(g(x)=\tfrac14-x^2\) satisfies
\[
L_y(g)=\tfrac14y_0-y_2=-\tfrac34<0.
\]
Every positive measure supported on \(K\) integrates \(g\) nonnegatively, so no \(K\)-representing measure exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The moments of equal mass at minus one and one are positive semidefinite but cannot be represented by a measure supported on the smaller interval.
assumptions_latex: Representing measures are finite positive Borel measures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sequence is globally representable but has no representing measure supported on \(K\).

notation.meaning: Riesz functional determined by the truncated moments

knowledge_statements.title: Nonextendable Truncated Moment Data
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive lower-order data whose prescribed higher odd moment prevents any positive extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define univariate truncated data through degree three by
\[
y_0=1,
\qquad y_1=0,
\qquad y_2=0,
\qquad y_3=1.
\]
Then \(M_1(y)=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}\succeq0\). Any extension through degree four would require
\[
M_2(y)=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&0&1\\0&1&y_4\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.
\]
This is impossible for every \(y_4\in\mathbb R\), since its principal submatrix \(\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&y_4\end{pmatrix}\) has determinant \(-1\). Thus the positive lower-order moment matrix does not admit a positive moment-matrix extension consistent with the prescribed degree-three datum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero second moment combined with a nonzero third moment yields a positive lower-order moment matrix but prevents every positive extension.
assumptions_latex: Positive extension means that the next Hankel moment matrix is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No choice of \(y_4\) makes the prescribed truncated data extend to \(M_2(y)\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: univariate Hankel moment matrix of order k

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), let
\[
K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:g_j(x)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}
\]
and
\[
Q(g)=\left\{\sigma_0+\sum_{j=1}^m\sigma_jg_j:\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_m\text{ are sums of squares}\right\}.
\]
The presentation is Archimedean when \(R-\|x\|_2^2\in Q(g)\) for some \(R>0\). If no such \(R\) exists, Putinar's Positivstellensatz does not supply the implication
\[
p>0\text{ on }K\quad\Longrightarrow\quad p\in Q(g)
\]
for \(p\in\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\). Consequently, monotone convergence of the associated moment-SOS bounds cannot be inferred from that theorem, even when \(K\) is compact under a different presentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without an Archimedean quadratic module, Putinar's positivity certificate and the usual hierarchy-convergence argument do not apply to that presentation; this alone does not establish divergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Non-Archimedean Presentation Failure

children.title: Escape of Mass or Minimizers to Infinity

knowledge_statements.title: Escape of Mass or Minimizers to Infinity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noncoercive polynomial optimization with unattained infimum and escaping minimizing measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[
f(x,y)=(xy-1)^2+x^2
\]
on \(\mathbb R^2\). Since \(f\ge0\), its infimum is nonnegative. Along \((x_t,y_t)=(t^{-1},t)\), one has \(f(x_t,y_t)=t^{-2}\to0\), so \(\inf f=0\). No finite point attains zero: \(f(x,y)=0\) would require simultaneously \(x=0\) and \(xy=1\). The minimizing sequence is unbounded, and the Dirac measures \(\delta_{(x_t,y_t)}\) are not tight. Their moments involving \(y\) diverge, preventing convergence to a finite representing measure for an optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial can have infimum zero only along an unbounded sequence, causing minimizing Dirac mass and its moments to escape to infinity.
assumptions_latex: Minimizing measures are probability measures, including Dirac measures at candidate points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The infimum is \(0\), is unattained, and admits an escaping minimizing sequence with no tight subsequence.

notation.meaning: explicit unbounded minimizing sequence
Dirac probability measure at the minimizing point

knowledge_statements.title: Hierarchy Dual Nonattainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-valued nonattainment of the SOS dual, excluding dual infeasibility and unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_d\) be the feasible set of the order-\(d\) SOS dual, with each \((\lambda,q)\in D_d\) consisting of a scalar lower bound \(\lambda\) and a tuple \(q\) of the required degree-bounded SOS multipliers. knowledge_statements.title: Hierarchy Gap–Attainment Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates equality of finite-order values from existence of primal and dual optimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite order-\(d\) values \(d_d\le p_d\), let \(\mathcal P_d^\star\) and \(\mathcal D_d^\star\) denote the primal and dual optimizer sets. The gap-attainment status is determined by the value predicate \(p_d=d_d\) and the attainment predicates \(\mathcal P_d^\star\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal D_d^\star\ne\varnothing\). Zero gap means only \(p_d=d_d\); it does not imply either attainment predicate. A positive gap means \(p_d>d_d\), independently of whether \(\mathcal P_d^\star\) or \(\mathcal D_d^\star\) is nonempty. Strong finite-order primal-dual solvability requires all three predicates simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero duality gap and attainment are separate properties; strong finite-order solvability requires equal values and optimizers on both sides.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semialgebraic dimension of the global minimizer set, not merely nonuniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a polynomial \(f\) on a semialgebraic feasible set \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \[f^*:=\min_{x\in K}f(x),\qquad Z^*:=\{x\in K:f(x)=f^*\}.\] The problem has a positive-dimensional minimizer set when the semialgebraic dimension satisfies \(\dim Z^*>0\). Equivalently, the minimizers are not a zero-dimensional semialgebraic set. This condition precludes representing the entire minimizer set by finitely many atoms, although particular optimal measures may still have finite support and finite hierarchy convergence may still occur for other reasons.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The global minimizers form a semialgebraic set of dimension at least one, rather than a finite or zero-dimensional set.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Dimensional Minimizer Sets

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An ordered family of variable cliques \((I_k)_{k=1}^s\) has the running-intersection property if, for every \(k\ge2\), there exists \(p(k)<k\) such that \[I_k\cap\bigcup_{j<k}I_j\subseteq I_{p(k)}.\] Running-intersection failure occurs when at least one \(k\ge2\) admits no such preceding clique. The failure removes the clique-tree consistency structure normally used to glue compatible local moment data and to establish convergence of standard correlative-sparsity hierarchies.

knowledge_statements.title: Inconsistent Local Moment Data
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise disagreement of local truncated moments on clique overlaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a relaxation order \(d\in\mathbb N\). Let \(y^{(k)}\) and \(y^{(\ell)}\) be truncated local moment sequences through degree \(2d\) on cliques \(I_k\) and \(I_\ell\). They are overlap-consistent through degree \(2d\) when \[y^{(k)}_\alpha=y^{(\ell)}_\alpha\quad\text{for every }\alpha\in\mathbb N^n\text{ with }|\alpha|\le2d\text{ and }\operatorname{supp}(\alpha)\subseteq I_k\cap I_\ell.\] Inconsistent local moment data occur when this equality fails for at least one clique pair and shared monomial. Such data cannot be restrictions of a single global truncated moment sequence having those local marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local moment vectors are inconsistent when they assign different values to the same shared monomial on an overlapping variable set.
assumptions_latex: Each clique \(I_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) carries a local moment sequence \(y^{(k)}\) indexed through degree \(2d\).
For each pair of cliques, moments whose multi-indices are supported on the overlap can be compared.

children.title: Numerical Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Finite-precision obstacles in solving and interpreting moment relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioned Moment Matrices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral perturbation boundary for finite truncated moment matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_d(y)=(y_{\alpha+\beta})_{|\alpha|,|\beta|\le d}\succeq0\), and let \(\lambda_{\min}^+(M_d(y))\) be its smallest positive eigenvalue. Define \(\kappa_+(M_d(y))=\|M_d(y)\|_2/\lambda_{\min}^+(M_d(y))\). If the matrix data are uncertain by relative spectral norm \(\varepsilon\) and \(\kappa_+(M_d(y))\varepsilon\ge1\), then an admissible symmetric perturbation can annihilate a positive eigenvalue or move it below zero. Consequently, positive semidefiniteness, kernel dimension, and rank inferred at that accuracy are not robust; exact moment or flatness conclusions cannot be certified from the perturbed matrix alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When relative data error exceeds the smallest positive eigenvalue scale, admissible perturbations can alter positivity, kernel, and rank, invalidating numerical moment and flatness conclusions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \kappa_+(M_d(y))\varepsilon\ge1\Longrightarrow\text{spectral rank and positivity are not robust}

notation.meaning: degree-d truncated moment matrix
condition number restricted to the positive spectrum
relative spectral-norm uncertainty

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits this numerical-failure leaf, and the spectral perturbation claim is mathematically plausible. However, the record provides no citation for the perturbation threshold or for its consequence for moment-matrix flatness and certification. The listed local moment reference does not by itself support the numerical conditioning claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Ambiguous Numerical Rank
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold stability criterion for numerical ranks used in flatness tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a symmetric matrix \(M\) with ordered eigenvalues \(\lambda_1\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_N\), define \(\operatorname{rank}_\tau(M)=\#\{i:\lambda_i(M)>\tau\}\). Suppose the computed matrix equals \(M+E\), where \(\|E\|_2\le\delta\). A claimed numerical rank \(r\) is invariant under every admissible perturbation if \(\lambda_r(M)>\tau+\delta\) and \(\lambda_{r+1}(M)<\tau-\delta\), with the endpoint conventions \(\lambda_0=+\infty\) and \(\lambda_{N+1}=-\infty\). If an eigenvalue lies in \([\tau-\delta,\tau+\delta]\), admissible perturbations can place it on either side of the threshold, so rank-based flatness is ambiguous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Numerical rank is stable only when the spectrum has a gap wider than the perturbation uncertainty around the chosen threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda_i(M)\in[\tau-\delta,\tau+\delta]\Longrightarrow\operatorname{rank}_\tau(M+E)\text{ is not perturbation-invariant}

notation.meaning: number of eigenvalues strictly exceeding the threshold
numerical-rank threshold
absolute spectral-norm uncertainty

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the terminal container. A Weyl-type perturbation source and a flatness-test source are required. In addition, the closed interval claim is not correct as written for the strict rule rank_tau(M)=#{i:lambda_i>tau}: when lambda_i=tau-delta, a perturbation of norm at most delta can reach tau but cannot place that eigenvalue strictly above tau. Source-backed correction of the endpoint convention is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Spurious or Unstable Extraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instability boundary for atom extraction through moment-matrix pseudoinverses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) index a basis selected from a moment matrix, let \(G=M_B(y)\), and let multiplication matrices be computed as \(X_i(y)=G^\dagger H_i(y)\). Atom extraction uses joint eigenvalues of the matrices \(X_i(y)\). If a sequence \(y^{(k)}\to y\) satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}G(y^{(k)})\ne\operatorname{rank}G(y)\), then the Moore–Penrose inverse, and hence the extraction map, need not be continuous. Even at fixed rank, small perturbations may be amplified when \(\sigma_{	min}(G)\) is small. Without a certified rank gap and small multiplication residuals, extracted atoms or weights may therefore be spurious or unstable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extraction can become discontinuous when the selected moment block changes rank, and near-singularity amplifies errors in multiplication matrices, atoms, and weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}M_B(y^{(k)})\not\to\operatorname{rank}M_B(y)\Longrightarrow X_i(y^{(k)})\not\to X_i(y)\text{ may occur}

notation.meaning: basis-indexed principal moment block
shifted moment block for multiplication by the ith coordinate
Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse of G

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind is appropriate, but the mathematical version is not ready for revision without sources. The expression \sigma_{\tmin}(G) contains the invalid command \tmin, the rank-change condition is expressed inconsistently between the statement and conclusion, and 'small multiplication residuals' is not defined. A numerical pseudoinverse source and a moment-atom extraction stability source are needed.

knowledge_statements.title: Weakly Feasible Moment SDPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak feasibility relative to the displayed semidefinite formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a moment relaxation with feasible set \(F=\{y:\mathcal A y=b,\ M_d(y)\succeq0,\ M_{d-d_j}(g_jy)\succeq0\ \text{for }j=1,\ldots,m\}\). It is weakly feasible in the displayed formulation when \(F\ne\varnothing\) but no feasible \(y\) makes every displayed semidefinite block positive definite. Equivalently, each feasible point lies on the boundary of at least one displayed positive-semidefinite cone. This definition is formulation-dependent: facial reduction may expose a smaller cone in which the same feasible set has a relative-interior point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A moment SDP is weakly feasible when it has feasible points but none strictly satisfies every displayed semidefinite constraint; facial reduction may restore relative strict feasibility.
assumptions_latex: M_d(y)\text{ and }M_{d-d_j}(g_jy)\text{ are symmetric affine matrix maps}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\ne\varnothing\quad\text{and}\quad\nexists y\in F\text{ with all displayed blocks positive definite}

notation.meaning: feasible set of the moment relaxation
moment matrix
localizing matrix associated with constraint polynomial g_j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the leaf if the project uses 'weakly feasible' to mean feasible but not strictly feasible in the displayed product cone. That terminology is not universal, and no conic-optimization source is cited. The formulation dependence and facial-reduction statement also require a specific authoritative locator.

children.title: Solver Accuracy Loss
children.top_down_role: Finite-precision regimes producing unreliable residuals, bounds, or certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Solver Accuracy Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-to-solution error boundary for numerical moment-SDP solvers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_*\) satisfy a locally differentiable primal-dual system \(F(z_*)=0\), and let a solver return \(\widehat z\) with residual \(\|F(\widehat z)\|\le\eta\). If the Jacobian \(J=DF(z_*)\) is nonsingular, local error scales as \(\|\widehat z-z_*\|=O(\|J^{-1}\|\eta)\), not merely as \(O(\eta)\). Thus, when \(\|J^{-1}\|\eta\) is comparable to the required accuracy, a small reported KKT residual does not certify accurate moments, objective values, or spectra. Near weak feasibility or loss of strict complementarity, \(J\) may become singular, eliminating a uniform residual-to-error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small KKT residuals need not mean accurate moments when the primal-dual system is ill-conditioned; near degeneracy, no uniform error bound may exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|J^{-1}\|\eta\not\ll1\Longrightarrow\text{small residual alone does not certify solution accuracy}

notation.meaning: primal-dual residual mapping
Jacobian of the residual mapping at the solution
reported residual tolerance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind matches the container, but the residual-to-error estimate requires the returned point to lie in a sufficiently small neighborhood of z_* and an explicitly local asymptotic regime. The assertions connecting weak feasibility or loss of strict complementarity to singularity of this unspecified residual Jacobian depend on the precise KKT formulation and need an SDP sensitivity source.

children.title: Feasibility–Accuracy Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Cases where numerical evidence cannot cleanly separate weak feasibility from solver error.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility–Accuracy Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance boundary separating approximate acceptance from exact SDP feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an affine moment-SDP system, define \(R(y)=\max\{\|\mathcal Ay-b\|,[-\lambda_{\min}(M_d(y))]_+,\max_j[-\lambda_{\min}(M_{d-d_j}(g_jy))]_+\}\). A tolerance-based solver accepts \(y\) whenever \(R(y)\le\tau\). If \(0<\inf_yR(y)\le\tau\), the exact system is infeasible although approximate points pass the test. Conversely, for a weakly feasible system, perturbations of size comparable to \(\tau\) can produce small negative eigenvalues and apparent infeasibility. Therefore, without a rigorous feasibility certificate or an infeasibility lower bound exceeding \(\tau\), solver status cannot distinguish exact feasibility from tolerance-scale error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the best constraint residual is no larger than solver tolerance, acceptance cannot prove exact feasibility, while weakly feasible problems may also appear infeasible after tiny perturbations.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal Ay=b\text{ and all semidefinite blocks define the exact system}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0<\inf_yR(y)\le\tau\Longrightarrow\text{tolerance acceptance does not imply exact feasibility}

notation.meaning: maximum equality and semidefinite feasibility violation
positive part max(a,0)
solver feasibility tolerance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits this leaf, and the implication 0<inf_y R(y)<=tau correctly shows that tolerance acceptance need not establish exact feasibility. However, the converse discussion does not specify whether the perturbations affect problem data, iterates, or computed spectra, and its connection to weak feasibility is not established by a cited source. A rigorous SDP feasibility and perturbation reference is required.
